item.title: Schneider Electric va racheter le spécialiste US des logiciels industriels PTC
item.description: Schneider Electric a annoncé lundi l'acquisition de 100% du capital du spécialiste des logiciels industriels américian PTC, au prix de 205 dollars (183 euros) par action.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Schneider Electric (SCHN.PA) a annoncé lundi l'acquisition de 100% du capital du spécialiste des logiciels industriels américian PTC, au prix de 205 dollars (183 euros) par action. Le fabricant français d'équipements électriques précise dans un communiqué que le but de ce rachat est de créer "une plateforme de logiciels industriels et d’intelligence artificielle de premier plan". Cette nouvelle acquisition de Schneider vient quelques mois après la conclusion, en juin, d'un accord pour racheter [USN:FWN43213W TEXT:"Cognite Holding"], un fournisseur privé de logiciels d’intelligence artificielle et de données industrielles. La finalisation de la transaction, évoquée par une source [USN:L8N45R00E TEXT:"peu avant"] son annonce, est prévue d'ici au troisième trimestre 2027. Elle valorise les capitaux propres de PTC à environ 22,6 milliards de dollars (et une valeur d'entreprise de 23,7 milliards de dollars). Schneider vise de réaliser 250 millions d'euros de synergies de coûts annuelles, reposant sur un plan d'exécution identifié et devant être atteintes d’ici trois ans, ainsi qu'environ 800 millions d’euros de synergies de revenus.

item.title: El ejército de EEUU dice que atacó una embarcación en el Caribe, matando a cuatro personas
item.description: El ejército de Estados Unidos dijo el domingo de que cuatro personas habían perdido la vida en un ataque a una embarcación en el mar Caribe, el último de una serie de ataques que, según Washington, tienen como objetivo a "narcoterroristas", pero que los expertos en derechos humanos consideran ejecuciones extrajudiciales.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh
item.content:encoded: El ejército de Estados Unidos dijo el domingo de que cuatro personas habían perdido la vida en un ataque a una embarcación en el mar Caribe, el último de una serie de ataques que, según Washington, tienen como objetivo a "narcoterroristas", pero que los expertos en derechos humanos consideran ejecuciones extrajudiciales. El Mando Sur de EEUU dijo en la red social X que "llevó a cabo un ataque letal y cinético contra una lancha rápida que operaba a lo largo de rutas establecidas de narcotráfico en el Caribe". Citó lo que denominó "información de inteligencia confirmada" para alegar la participación activa de la embarcación en el narcotráfico, sin aportar más detalles. Añadió que cuatro personas, a las que calificó de "narcoterroristas", resultaron muertas. El Gobierno del presidente Donald Trump ha afirmado que las embarcaciones contra las que ha atacado desde septiembre de 2025 transportaban narcóticos. Los ataques estadounidenses contra este tipo de embarcaciones en el Caribe y el Pacífico oriental han acabado con la vida de más de 220 personas. Expertos y defensores de los derechos humanos, tanto en EEUU como en el extranjero, han cuestionado la legalidad de los ataques. Human Rights Watch, Amnistía Internacional y expertos independientes de la ONU han calificado los ataques de ejecuciones extrajudiciales ilegales. Ben Saul, relator especial de la ONU sobre derechos humanos y lucha contra el terrorismo, ha afirmado que existen "motivos razonables para creer" que dichos ataques "constituyeron crímenes contra la humanidad por asesinato según el derecho internacional consuetudinario". La Unión Estadounidense por las Libertades Civiles ha calificado las afirmaciones del Gobierno de Trump contra aquellos a quienes tiene en el punto de mira de "afirmaciones sin fundamento y alarmistas".

item.title: Taipei mayor defends city's inclusivity after gay bar raid sparks protests
item.description: Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an on Monday defended the city as welcoming and inclusive after a police raid of a gay bar sparked protests by the LGBTQ+ community over alleged discrimination and official misconduct.
item.dc:creator: Ben Blanchard, Yimou Lee
item.content:encoded: Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an on Monday defended the city as welcoming and inclusive after a police raid of a gay bar sparked protests by the LGBTQ+ community over alleged discrimination and official misconduct. One video of the weekend raid that circulated on social media showed a police officer asking a customer in a wheelchair who was in the toilet how disabled people "manage to have sex in there". Chiang, who faces reelection next month, said he deeply regretted "improper conduct" by police. Taiwan legalised same-sex marriage in 2019 in a first for Asia and is normally a bastion of tolerance in a region where LGBTQ+ rights are often suppressed or outlawed. Taipei holds its main Pride event later this month, the largest in East Asia. Taipei police raided the Commander D bar in the city's main gay neighbourhood of Ximen on Saturday afternoon, citing a complaint alleging the bar could be violating public decency laws. They took 51 people in for questioning and arrested the owner. Police said on Sunday they had taken disciplinary action against officers for "inappropriate conduct" during the operation, without elaborating. Chiang, who has previously attended Taipei Pride, said regardless of age, gender, sexual orientation, identity, ethnicity or beliefs, the government must ensure everyone in Taipei enjoys equal rights. "Taipei has always been an inclusive and friendly city for us," he said. Chiang, of the opposition Kuomintang, is locked in a tight election race against Puma Shen of the ruling Democratic Progressive Party. Shen said in a Facebook post on Monday that while any illegality should be handled according to the law, people's rights and dignity should be respected. "Taipei's diversity and inclusivity should not only be visible on Pride parade day," he wrote. RIGHTS GROUPS ANGERED The Commander D raid was one of three operations on Saturday involving Ximen gay bars, police precinct spokesperson Chen Yu-cheng told Reuters. Police had in the past conducted "irregular inspections" of the three venues, he said. Chen added that the precinct inspected 15 entertainment venues on Saturday. Rights groups say there is a deeper problem. "This was not a case of individual officers misspeaking or a single instance of excessive enforcement, but the resurfacing of long-standing homophobia, discrimination and abuse of power within the police enforcement system," the Taiwan Alliance to Promote Civil Partnership Rights said in a joint statement with other groups condemning the raid. One person among the 51 taken in for questioning said they had been detained for more than six hours after police accused them of violating a law that prohibits "wantonly exposing one's naked body or presenting a lascivious posture in a public place." The person, who requested anonymity, said they had removed their shirt only shortly before police arrived because the bar was crowded and hot. "I trusted the police to know the law," the person said. "So when they told me I had broken the law by not wearing a shirt in a public place and had to pay a fine, I did not challenge them." Lead investigator Chen Yi-kai told Reuters shirtless people were taken in because officers had found evidence of sexual or obscene conduct but could not immediately determine who was involved, adding that police were inclined not to fine the 51 people.

item.content:encoded: Die Stimmung in der deutschen Automobilindustrie hat sich im September stark eingetrübt. Das Barometer für das Geschäftsklima fiel auf minus 35,0 Punkte, von minus 22,0 Zählern im August, wie das Münchner Ifo-Institut am Montag zu seiner Umfrage mitteilte. Die Unternehmen bewerteten ihre Geschäftslage so schlecht wie noch nie in diesem Jahr. Die Aussichten für die kommenden Monate waren schon im August drastisch gesunken und verharrten nun auf tiefem Niveau. "Die Automobilindustrie steckt weiterhin in der Krise", sagte Ifo-Branchenexpertin Anita Wölfl. Diese Krisenstimmung lässt sich an vielen weiteren Indikatoren erkennen: So sackten die Exporterwartungen in der Autoindustrie ab, nachdem sie zuvor noch gestiegen waren. Ähnliches galt für die Beschäftigungserwartungen. Die Unternehmen bewerteten im September überdies ihren Auftragsbestand erneut schlechter als im Vormonat. Die Ertragslage, die immer vierteljährlich abgefragt wird, ist den Unternehmensangaben zufolge im dritten Quartal im Vergleich zum Vorquartal deutlich gesunken. In anderen Industriezweigen wie der Elektro- und der Chemieindustrie hat sich die Stimmung zuletzt merklich aufgehellt. Ein Grund für die Schwäche der Autobranche ist die wachsende Konkurrenz aus China, etwa bei Elektrofahrzeugen. Die chinesischen Autobauer drängen mit Macht auf den europäischen Markt, weil der eigene Markt schwächelt und es eine enorme Überproduktion gibt. Der US-Markt ist ihnen aufgrund der Handelspolitik versperrt. Die deutsche Autoindustrie lehnt deshalb Importzölle nicht mehr generell ab. Priorität müsse aber weiter die Stärkung der eigenen Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und ein Dialog mit China als Handelspartner haben, erklärte die Chefin des Verbandes der Automobilindustrie (VDA), Hildegard Müller, kürzlich.

item.content:encoded: Alle europäischen Autobauer schaffen einer Studie zufolge die CO2-Grenzwerte der Europäischen Union. Schon jetzt hätten die Hersteller die Vorgaben zu 75 Prozent erfüllt, hieß es in einer Studie der Lobbyorganisation Transport & Environment, die am Montag veröffentlicht wurde. Für die vollständige Umsetzung haben sie bis Ende 2027 Zeit. Es sei damit zu rechnen, dass viele Hersteller schon vor Ablauf der Frist zum Ziel kämen. "Die Anzeichen sind klar: Die CO2–Ziele funktionieren so wie erwartet", hieß es in der Untersuchung. Frühere Aussagen aus der Branche, dass die Vorgaben nicht erreicht werden könnten, hätten sich als falsch erwiesen. "Das Schlussquartal 2026 wird für die europäische Branche der Schlüsselmoment." Jetzt kämen die Verhandlungen zu den CO2-Zielen zum Abschluss. Die Verantwortlichen müssten entscheiden, ob die elektrische Zukunft Europas gesichert werde oder mit Alternativen wie Biofuels eine Sackgasse eingeschlagen werde. "Die Politiker müssen entschieden handeln, um die Bevölkerung zu schützen und diese zur letzten fossilen Energie-Krise zu machen." In den vergangenen Monaten schnellte der Absatz von Elektroautos in vielen europäischen Ländern nach oben. Dabei spielten die hohen Ölpreise und staatliche Kaufanreize eine wichtige Rolle. Dazu kommt eine zunehmende Auswahl insbesondere bei kleineren Fahrzeugen. Der Verkauf von Autos zum Preis von weniger als 25.000 Euro dürfte sich im laufenden Jahr um das Siebenfache im Vergleich zu 2024 erhöhen, hieß es in der T&E-Studie. Zuletzt hatte Volkswagen (VOWG.DE) den elektrischen Polo und drei Schwestermodelle in dieser Kategorie auf den Markt gebracht. Allerdings seien weiter mehr Verbrennerfahrzeuge in dieser Preiskategorie verfügbar. Überhaupt sei das laufende Jahr geprägt von einer Vielzahl neuer Fahrzeuge. Derzeit seien mehr als 150 Elektromodelle auf dem Markt, fast 40 davon seien in der ersten Jahreshälfte eingeführt worden. Angeführt werde diese Statistik von den europäischen Autobauern, die fast 60 Prozent der Fahrzeuge stellten. Chinesische Hersteller kämen auf 21 Prozent.

item.title: Russian air strikes targeted port infrastructure in Ukraine's Odesa region, governor says
item.description: Massive Russian air strikes targeted industrial and port infrastructure in Ukraine's Odesa region, Governor Oleh Kiper said on the Telegram messaging app on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Massive Russian air strikes targeted industrial and port infrastructure in Ukraine's Odesa region, Governor Oleh Kiper said on the Telegram messaging app on Monday. All of the fires caused have been extinguished so far, he added. A Russian air strike on Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-biggest city, killed one person and injured six others, Mayor Ihor Terekhov said on Telegram late on Sunday. The Russian defence ministry said on Telegram it hit Vylkove port, fuel depot facilities in Chornomorsk and cargo vessels, all in the Odesa region, as well as a power station in the Kharkiv region, which it said were used for military purposes.

item.title: Takaichi pledges fiscal discipline as Japan's debt bill rises
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Monday pledged to "control" bond issuance and act swiftly against market turbulence, seeking to reassure investors worried about Japan's worsening public finances that have pushed up bond yields.
item.dc:creator: Leika Kihara
item.content:encoded: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Monday pledged to "control" bond issuance and act swiftly against market turbulence, seeking to reassure investors worried about Japan's worsening public finances that have pushed up bond yields. She said the government would pursue fiscal sustainability even as it ramps up spending to bolster growth potential, including by reviewing existing tax breaks and subsidies. "Fiscal sustainability is obviously a prerequisite in pursuing our 'responsible and proactive' fiscal policy," Takaichi said in a policy speech to parliament. The remarks reflect mounting concern in Tokyo over rising Japanese government bond (JGB) yields, which would boost the cost of funding the premier's ambitious spending plans. The 30-year JGB yield hit a record high of 4.235% on Monday on jitters over the risk of increased debt issuance and inflation worries fuelled by the Middle East war. Japan's public debt, at roughly twice the size of its economy, is the largest in the developed world. Funding costs are climbing as the Bank of Japan raises interest rates and tapers bond purchases in an effort to wean the economy off decades of massive stimulus. Takaichi said the government will seek to draw in private investment in growth areas through "massive, long-term fiscal expenditure deployed in a well-planned, predictable manner." At the same time, it would keep a lid on annual bond issuance, calibrating borrowing to tax revenues, interest rates, debt-financing costs and economic and market developments, the premier said in the speech to an extraordinary parliament session that convened on Monday. "If the economy and markets make unexpected moves, we will scrutinise their impact and respond nimbly as needed," she added without elaborating. Fiscal policy is set to take centre stage in parliamentary debate in Japan as rising concerns over the fiscal health of advanced economies fuel a broader rise in global bond yields. The administration's immediate priority is passing legislation backing Takaichi's plan for a [USN:L1N457045 TEXT:"two-year tax cut"] on food items from next April, which sparked a bond selloff due to a lack of detail on how the revenue shortfall will be filled. The government is also preparing next year's budget, with ministries seeking record levels of spending. Separately, Takaichi said Tokyo will set aside multi-year funds for strategically important economic security initiatives. "We will implement policies steadily, get things done one by one, and communicate them carefully to the public and markets," Takaichi said.

item.title: Russia says it struck two Ukrainian cargo vessels in the Black Sea
item.description: The Russian defence ministry said on Monday its forces struck two Ukrainian cargo vessels in the Black Sea.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Russian defence ministry said on Monday its forces struck two Ukrainian cargo vessels in the Black Sea. It said it hit fuel storage facilities at the port of Chornomorsk that were intended to supply Ukrainian armed forces, as well as a dry cargo vessel carrying military equipment. Another dry cargo vessel transporting military supplies was hit south of the city of Odesa, according to a statement. It also said the Kochetok electrical substation was struck in the Kharkiv region.

item.title: New Zealand's Bracewell shifts to casual contract, eyes BBL opportunity
item.description: New Zealand all-rounder Michael Bracewell will move to a casual contract for the 2026-27 season as he pursues an opportunity in Australia's Big Bash League, the country's cricket board (NZC) said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New Zealand all-rounder Michael Bracewell will move to a casual contract for the 2026-27 season as he pursues an opportunity in Australia's Big Bash League, the country's cricket board (NZC) said on Monday. Bracewell, who has played 105 times for New Zealand across all three formats, will feature in the limited-overs series against India beginning this month. The 35-year-old joins [USN:L4N4500JN TEXT:"Mark Chapman"], Finn Allen, Lockie Ferguson, Adam Milne and Tim Seifert among players who have opted for the casual contract system, which allows them to play in high-paying Twenty20 leagues while remaining available for national duty. "As a white-ball only player, this felt like too good of an opportunity to pass up," Bracewell said in a statement. "I'm still very much committed to the Black Caps and can't wait to be involved in the upcoming India tour and future white-ball series." Batter Nick Kelly will replace Bracewell on NZC's central contract list.

item.content:encoded: OKXICE, the joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE.N) , filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Sunday to launch a tokenized securities platform for around-the-clock trading of US stocks. More than 60 listed companies will be available for around-the-clock trading throughout the week, according to the filing "This is a landmark step toward a truly global, 24/7 Wall Street," said former New York Governor Andrew Cuomo, who is co-chair of OKXICE, in a post on the X social media platform The SEC unveiled an [USN:L6N4590SA TEXT:"exemption"] last month allowing companies to offer trading in blockchain-based or "tokenized" stocks and other securities. The move came two days after comprehensive cryptocurrency legislation backed by US President Donald Trump [USN:L1N4570IP TEXT:"failed to advance"] in the Senate Global exchanges including the NYSE, Nasdaq and the London Stock Exchange are preparing to launch round-the-clock trading in the coming months Prediction markets' push into US stock trading has recently raised [USN:L6N44114G TEXT:"regulatory concerns"]

item.title: NHL roundup: Mikael Granlund's OT goal hands Ducks win over Panthers
item.description: Mikael Granlund's power-play goal with 46 seconds left in overtime gave the host Anaheim Ducks a 3-2 win over the Florida Panthers on Sunday night.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Mikael Granlund's power-play goal with 46 seconds left in overtime gave the host Anaheim Ducks a 3-2 win over the Florida Panthers on Sunday night. Granlund tipped in Carlsson's pass from the right corner for the winner, helping Anaheim win its first home game of the season. Cutter Gauthier had two goals and an assist for the Ducks, who scored all three of their goals with the man advantage. Leo Carlsson contributed three assists and Lukas Dostal made 29 saves. Carter Verhaeghe and Brad Marchand, making his season debut, got the goals for the Panthers, who have played into overtime in all three of their games this season. Jacob Markstrom stopped 18 shots. Jets 3, Red Wings 2 Kyle Connor scored two power-play goals and added an assist to lift Winnipeg to a 3-2 victory over host Detroit. Cole Perfetti scored the other goal and had two assists, while Josh Morrissey added two assists for the Jets, who went 3-for-4 on the power play. Stuart Skinner made 33 saves in Winnipeg's first victory of the season. Viktor Arvidsson and Emmitt Finnie scored for the Red Wings, and John Gibson stopped 24 shots. Rangers 4, Mammoth 2 Gabe Perreault scored the tiebreaking goal 3:15 into New York's three-goal third period during a win against visiting Utah. Vladislav Gavrikov had a goal and an assist for the Rangers, who won their third straight. Igor Shesterkin made 28 saves in the victory and got the secondary assist on Tolvanen's empty-net goal with 1:15 remaining. Nick Schmaltz scored Utah's sixth power-play goal through the team's first three games with 5:31 left in the second. Clayton Keller assisted on the goal, extending his regular-season point streak to 13 games. Golden Knights 3, Canucks 2 Marc Gatcomb scored the go-ahead goal late in the second period and Adin Hill made 18 saves to lead Vegas past host Vancouver. Mitch Marner and Victor Olofsson also scored goals for the Golden Knights, who improved to 22-4-3 all-time against the Canucks, including the last eight in a row. Hill, making his first start for Vegas since April 9 of last season, extended his personal win streak against Vancouver to five straight games. Paul Cotter and Jonathan Lekkerimaki scored goals for Vancouver, which was playing the second game of a back-to-back that began with a 4-1 home victory over Calgary on Saturday. Kevin Lankinen stopped 25 of 28 shots for the Canucks. Kraken 6, Flames 1 Mackie Samoskevich scored twice and Berkly Catton had a goal and an assist as Seattle convincingly won its home opener over Calgary. Bobby McMann, Shane Wright and Jordan Eberle also scored, and Chandler Stephenson and Brandon Montour had two assists apiece for the Kraken, who rebounded from a 3-1 loss Saturday in Edmonton. Goaltender Joey Daccord made 32 saves. Morgan Frost scored and Dustin Wolf stopped 21 of 27 shots for the Flames, who have been outscored 16-3 across their three losses to begin the season. --Field Level Media

item.title: European EV sales hit record in 'pivotal' year for affordable cars, study shows
item.description: Europe's uptake of electric vehicles is gaining momentum, with record sales so far this year driven by a slew of affordable models coming onto the market to bring carmakers in line with EU targets, according to a study.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Europe's uptake of electric vehicles is gaining momentum, with record sales so far this year driven by a slew of affordable models coming onto the market to bring carmakers in line with EU targets, according to a study. EV sales across the EU reached record volumes in 2026, with 1.64 million sold in the January-to-August period, up 45% year-on-year, Brussels-based environmental advocacy group Transport & Environment found in its EV progress report published on Monday. EVs made up 22% of the market during this period, six points higher than the same period last year, according to the report. T&E called 2026 "a pivotal year for EV availability", with model choice up 50% in a single year as carmakers expand their line-ups to meet EU emissions targets. The report comes as carmakers like Volkswagen roll out a number of affordable EVs, such as the all-electric Polo, helping the German auto group to close its existing compliance gap and avoid fines. European carmakers dominated the EV offering with nearly 60% of available models, adding 16 in the first half of 2026. Chinese carmakers held 21% and added 11 models. The study also noted the impact of rising fuel prices linked to the Middle East conflict on drivers of combustion-engine cars. Diesel has risen the most, up 38% since the Iran war began, with a 50-litre tank now costing €30 ($34) more, it said. ($1 = €0.8890)

item.title: For freed Israeli hostages, every moment is now precious
item.description: Taken with their children or alone. Held for weeks, months or years. Confined in captors' homes or Hamas tunnels as war raged above them. Israeli former hostages seized on October 7 say they now cherish even the smallest moments of freedom.
item.dc:creator: Shir Torem, Hannah Confino
item.content:encoded:
Aviva Siegel, 65, embraces her husband Keith Siegel, 67, both former hostages, as they watch the sunset from a field near their home in Kibbutz Gazit, northern Israel, August 6, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Hamas' October 7, 2023 attack was Israel's single deadliest day. The militants rampaged through villages, a music festival and army bases, killing 1,200 people and dragging 251 hostages back to Gaza. They included civilians, soldiers, men, women, children and elderly people, Israelis and foreign nationals. Most were freed in return for Palestinian prisoners during ceasefires between Israel and Hamas, but dozens did not survive.

Emily Damari, 30

British-Israeli Emily Damari, 30, a former hostage, models during a photo shoot for her clothing brand which carries the slogan 'never lose yourself' and which, according to Emily, helps her manage her trauma by giving her purpose and a way to support her future and rehabilitation journey, in Tel Aviv, Israel, July 28, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

"Freedom has completely changed the way I see life," said Emily Damari, 30, who was abducted wounded from her home in Kibbutz Kfar Aza and released in January 2025.

Palestinian Hamas militants hand over Emily Damari to members of the International Committee of the Red Cross in Gaza City, January 19, 2025. REUTERS/Dawoud Abu Alkas/File Photo Emily Damari was abducted from her home in Kibbutz Kfar Aza after being shot in the hand and injured; she was held for 471 days before being released in January 2025. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Her ordeal taught her not to take anything for granted, she said. "One day in captivity feels like one week. You want to give up at every moment, but I did not," said Damari, who has recently married and launched a clothing line in Israel. "Today, I open the fridge and I say thank you. I drink cold water and I say thank you. I am thankful for everything, big things and little things. Gratitude has become central to who I am," said Damari. "Being free, at home, surrounded by my family and my people is something I will never take for granted again."

Emily Damari looks in the mirror during a photo shoot for her clothing brand in Tel Aviv, Israel, July 28, 2026. "Freedom has completely changed the way I see life." REUTERS/Shir Torem

Emily Hand, 11

Emily Hand, 11, practices surfing through therapeutic surfing NGO HaGal Sheli, on Zikim beach in southern Israel, June 16, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Emily Hand was abducted from a friend's home in Kibbutz Beeri while staying there for a sleepover, along with her friend Hila Rotem and Hila's mother. REUTERS/Shir Torem Emily and and her friend Hila were taken to Gaza and held for 50 days before being released in November 2023. REUTERS/Shir Torem

I am trying to move on with my life. You can't just say 'it happened and it's over and that's it'. It happened but I am trying to detach from it. (When I surf) it's only me and the sea. I'm thinking of nothing else, only concentrating on the surf. Just me, the sea and the surfboard. Emily Hand, 11, seized from Be'eri, released November 25 2023

Emily's father said that his daughter, who was 8 years old when she was taken hostage, could only speak in whispers following her release. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Eli Shararbi, 54

Eli Sharabi, 54, sits on a sofa during a tour of Shalva, a disability care and inclusion center in Jerusalem, July 30, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Eli Sharabi, 54, was seized from nearby Kibbutz Be'eri. His British-born wife Lianne and their two daughters Noiya, 16, and Yahel, 13, were slain by the attackers. His brother Yossi was taken hostage and killed in Gaza. In February 2025, Sharabi was released, appearing emaciated and skeletally thin, from 491 days of captivity which he says included being held in a tunnel, hungry, shackled and beaten.

Eli Sharabi is released by Hamas militants after 491 days in captivity, in the central Gaza Strip, February 8, 2025. REUTERS/Hatem Khaled/File Photo Eli Sharabi laughs during a tour of Shalva, a disability care and inclusion center he is establishing in Jerusalem. REUTERS/Shir Torem

"I learned in captivity how precious every moment and every choice can be, and I carry that understanding with me now. I choose to look ahead, to keep going and to use the life I have in a meaningful way," said Sharabi. Since his release he has helped establish the Shalva Sharabi Family Centre in the southern city of Ashkelon with the disability charity Shalva, to treat families coping with trauma and disabilities, in commemoration of his own family lost. "I choose life. I choose to keep living fully, while carrying Lianne, Noiya, Yahel and Yossi with me in everything I do." His wife and daughters believed deeply in caring for others, he said. "Their kindness and care for others will continue. Families will walk through these doors and receive help, care and hope in a place that carries their name. That gives me strength and makes me very proud," said Sharabi.

Eli Sharabi looks up at a banner depicting himself and his slain wife, Lianne, and daughters Noiya and Yahel at Shalva, the disability care and inclusion center he is establishing in Jerusalem, July 30, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Doron Steinbrecher, 32

Doron Steinbrecher, 32, watches the sunset with her beloved dog, Pal, on a beach in Shefayim, Israel, August 12, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Hamas militants hand over Doron Steinbrecher, held in captivity for 471 days, to members of the International Committee of the Red Cross in Gaza City, January 19, 2025. REUTERS/via Reuters TV/File Photo Doron Steinbrecher was abducted from her home in Kibbutz Kfar Aza after calling her parents to tell them she was scared and that gunmen had arrived at her building; she was taken hostage to Gaza and held for 471 days before being released in January 2025. REUTERS/Shir Torem

What gives me strength today are my friends, family, and even my dog. The people who fought for me to be here and want to see me heal, be happy, and fulfill myself. Every day is a reminder of how nothing can be taken for granted and that I received my life as a gift, so I have to make the most of it and do everything that makes me feel good. Doron Steinbrecher, 33, seized from Kfar Aza, released January 2025

Doron Steinbrecher, 32, with her beloved dog, Pal, on a beach in Shefayim, Israel, August 12, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Hagar Brodutch, 43

Hagar Brodutch, 43, adds the final touches to a tart during a class at a culinary school where she is learning French pastry, in Tel Aviv, Israel, September 16, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Hagar Brodutch was seized from Kfar Aza with her three children and her neighbours' daughter who fled to their house after her parents were killed. They were freed in a brief truce in November 2023. Life after captivity, she said, can be far more complicated than sometimes portrayed. "The daily struggle is immense, especially for children. I believe it will take many more years before captivity becomes just a shadow that walks alongside us, rather than something that defines who we are," said Brodutch. Recently, Brodutch, 43, has begun taking classes in pastry baking, for which she has long had a passion. "This is about much more than learning how to bake. It is about finding a new path, creating something with my own hands, and slowly building a future," she said. "During my time in Hamas captivity, I began to understand that if I were released, returning to my previous life and working in management might no longer be possible," said Brodutch. "I chose pastry as a form of therapy, but also as a way to create something new for myself, with the hope that one day it could become my profession," she said.

Hagar was abducted from her home in Kibbutz Kfar Aza along with her three children, and their three-year-old neighbour; all five were taken hostage to Gaza and held for 51 days before being released in November 2023. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Agam Berger, 22

Agam Berger, 22, practices the violin ahead of performances at two memorial ceremonies for the third anniversary of October 7 at her home in Holon, Israel, September 17, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

What gives me strength is my family, the people of Israel, to be involved in meaningful activity and to give others the strength of hope. Agam Berger, 22, abducted from her military base near the Gaza border, released January 2025

Hamas militants release Israeli soldier Agam Berger in Gaza, January 30, 2025. REUTERS/Dawoud Abu Alkas/File Photo Agam Berger was abducted from the Nahal Oz military base in southern Israel, where she was serving as a surveillance soldier, and taken hostage to Gaza, where she was held for 482 days before being released in January 2025. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Aviva and Keith Siegel, 62 and 65

Aviva Siegel, 65, holds her husband Keith Siegel, 67, both former hostages, as they watch the sunset from a field near their home in Kibbutz Gazit, northern Israel, August 6, 2026. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Kfar Aza was one of the hardest-hit communities in Hamas' attack. Aviva Siegel, 62, was kidnapped with her husband Keith, 65. She was released in November 2023, but Keith was held until February 2025.

Aviva Siegel reacts following her release, in Ofakim, Israel, November 26, 2023. REUTERS/Amir Cohen/File Photo Aviva was released after 51 days, while Keith remained in captivity for 484 days before being released in February 2025. REUTERS/Shir Torem

Aviva joined the hostage release campaign movement in Israel while her husband was still being held. Their reunion and her children and grandchildren, and even strangers she meets, give her strength every day, she says. "I feel that I’m not alone and that there's so much love in this world and we need to keep it with both our hands," she said. "I feel very, very lucky to be alive."

Aviva Siegel, 65, and her husband Keith Siegel, 67, both former hostages, during a walk at sunset with two of their grandchildren near their home in Kibbutz Gazit, northern Israel, August 6, 2026. Aviva says her strength comes from having Keith by her side and being with her children and grandchildren. REUTERS/Shir Torem

item.title: Hong Kong stocks tick down in thin trade as property, financials drag
item.description: Hong Kong stocks edged lower in light trading on Monday, as selling pressure on property developers and financial heavyweights outweighed modest gains in tech shares.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Hong Kong stocks edged lower in light trading on Monday, as selling pressure on property developers and financial heavyweights outweighed modest gains in tech shares. ** Hong Kong benchmark Hang Seng (.HSI) was down 0.08% by midday, while the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index (.HSCE) was flat. ** Shares in rate-sensitive sectors continued to decline. ** Real estate firms (.HSNP) dropped 0.9% while a finance subindex tracking big banks and insurance firms (.HSNF) lost 0.7%. ** Hang Seng Tech (.HSTECH) meanwhile went up 0.3%. ** Semiconductor and PCB shares led the gain. Kingboard Laminates (1888.HK) surged 9% while Hua Hong Grace Semiconductor jumped 4%. ** China's onshore financial markets are closed from October 1 until October 7 for the National Day holidays. item.title: Japan has no plans for new oil release from national reserves, official says
item.description: Japanese Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said on Monday there were no plans for a fresh release of crude oil from national reserves as the country had already released supplies.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japanese Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said on Monday there were no plans for a fresh release of crude oil from national reserves as the country had already released supplies. Kihara's comments come even as the Group of Seven countries, of which Japan is a member, [USN:L6N45O0G5 TEXT:"agreed"] on Friday to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil from emergency reserves and pledged to refrain from energy export restrictions. The announcement followed [USN:L6N45N0J6 TEXT:"pressure"] from US President Donald Trump on the European Union to draw down emergency diesel inventories. It was uncertain how much of the new release would come from what remains from the 400 million barrels of oil that the 32 countries that are members of the International Energy Agency agreed to release in March to mitigate disruptions from the US-Israeli war on Iran. IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol said last week that members had released about two-thirds of the 400-million-barrel agreement. In March, Japan said it would release about 80 million barrels of oil from its reserves as part of the coordinated agreement. Japan also conducted a second round of national crude oil stockpile releases in May. "Japan has been releasing oil from reserves for some time now and there are no plans for a further release at this stage," Kihara told a press conference. The G7 meeting came amid delays in the release of European strategic reserves and growing concerns over soaring diesel prices globally, with discussions focusing in particular on measures to address diesel prices in Europe, the US and elsewhere, Kihara said.

item.title: England boss Tuchel says Scott can challenge Rice for midfield spot
item.description: England manager Thomas Tuchel said Declan Rice faces competition for his midfield spot after Alex Scott delivered an impressive performance on his first international start in Saturday's 7-0 thrashing of Croatia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: England manager Thomas Tuchel said Declan Rice faces competition for his midfield spot after Alex Scott delivered an impressive performance on his first international start in Saturday's [USN:L6N45P07T TEXT:"7-0"] thrashing of Croatia. With Rice having [USN:L1N45D0F0 TEXT:"withdrawn from the squad"], Bournemouth's Scott featured in midfield alongside Elliot Anderson for the Nations League match, and the pair dictated play despite being up against Croatian veterans Luka Modric and Mateo Kovacic. When asked if Arsenal's Rice might be worried about his place in the team, Tuchel told reporters: "Of course, and he does, we need performances like this. "This is just the nature of it. We will not survive on two central midfielders. "Declan knows about his importance, and he's one of the very best midfielders in Europe. "Nothing will change that. But it's exactly what we need. We need more, more, more, more variety. We need more, more, more options. Then it's always about the guys who are in camp. Alex was in the highest level." England, second in their group behind World Cup winners Spain, host the Czech Republic at Wembley on Tuesday.

item.title: Beijing park's holiday caterpillar hunt targets 'forest food monster'
item.description: For most families, China's "Golden Week" holiday is a time to relax, eat well, and visit the country's tourist hot spots.
item.dc:creator: Mandy Leong
item.content:encoded: For most families, China's "Golden Week" holiday is a time to relax, eat well, and visit the country's tourist hot spots. But at a wildlife park in Beijing, some people have been spending their holiday hunting for fall webworm larvae, an invasive species of caterpillar the park has dubbed "the forest food monster". Beijing Wildlife Park asked visitors to catch as many of the caterpillars as possible, rewarding those with the heaviest haul with prizes including as many as 10 park tickets. The caterpillar, native to North America, can damage more than 300 plant species including crops and fruit trees. After a crash course on how to spot the larvae, participants spread out across the nearly 550-acre (223-hectare) park with disposable gloves, plastic containers and chopsticks. "Call for warriors! Battle the 'forest food monster' and win grand prizes!" read a poster behind a table stacked with containers of crawling caterpillars. More than 310,000 caterpillars with a combined weight of 47.65 kg (105.05 lbs) have been caught by some 2,077 people since the competition began on September 28. The fall webworm is a major pest in China and produces three generations a year. Beijing is currently experiencing peak damage from this year's third generation of larvae, China's Xinhua news agency reported earlier this week, quoting the chief scientist at the Chinese Academy of Forestry. "(We've) noticed there are a lot of fall webworm larvae around us," said a 35-year-old participant surnamed Cui. "I think the Beijing Wildlife Park activity is very meaningful. It sparks the interest of our children, and (we) can even win a prize at the same time."

item.title: India, US have reached a plateau in trade talks, Indian finance minister says
item.description: India and the United States have reached a plateau in their trade deal talks, India's Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday, a further sign that the two sides have hit a wall on a crucial deal.
item.dc:creator: Shivangi Acharya
item.content:encoded: India and the United States have reached a plateau in their [USN:S0N40K049 TEXT:"trade deal talks,"] India's Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday, a further sign that the two sides have hit a wall on a crucial deal. Giving or taking more beyond that plateau would be "very, very difficult" for both countries, Sitharaman said at an event in New Delhi. "Maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it," she added. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said last week that an agreement was not imminent, after a meeting with Indian Trade Minister Piyush Goyal in the United States. "It's been a hard and very vigorously negotiated agreement. The negotiations are still ongoing," Sitharaman said. The two countries have been negotiating a trade agreement since February 2025 as they seek to deepen economic ties and resolve long-standing market access issues. Sitharaman said the trade balance between the two countries was in India's favour and the deficit was Washington's. "They would want to reduce that imbalance," she said. Reuters [USN:L1N43F08Q TEXT:"reported earlier"] this year that India was holding out for better terms in the trade deal with the US.

item.title: Gaw Capital seeks Hong Kong listing for real estate private debt fund
item.description: Gaw Capital plans to list a new Hong Kong fund that will invest in private loans backed by property assets across Asia Pacific and the Middle East, including but not limited to Japan, New Zealand, Singapore and South Korea, a draft listing document showed.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Gaw Capital plans to list a new Hong Kong fund that will invest in private loans backed by property assets across Asia Pacific and the Middle East, including but not limited to Japan, New Zealand, Singapore and South Korea, a draft listing document showed. Here are more details from the filing on Friday: Gaw Capital is a Hong Kong-based investment manager focused on real estate, private debt, infrastructure and growth equity. It managed about $35.6 billion in assets as of December 31, 2025. Financial details including the fundraising size and share price were not disclosed. The Gaw Capital Real Estate Private Debt OFC aims to give investors exposure to loans that are usually available mainly through private funds. It will target regular quarterly dividends and long-term gains. The fund plans to invest at least 90% of its assets in property related debt, including senior loans, construction loans and other secured financing. It can borrow up to 30% of its net asset value. The fund expects to invest 50% of the money raised within six months of listing and up to 100% within nine months. Jefferies is sole sponsor and joint listing agent, alongside CMB International.

item.content:encoded: Shares of AceVector, the parent company of Indian e-commerce platform Snapdeal, made a subdued debut on Monday, valuing the company at 12.96 billion Indian rupees ($134.7 million), as the absence of profitability offset its reasonable valuation. Here are more details: Shares of the SoftBank-backed (9984.T) company listed at 28.32 rupees on the National Stock Exchange of India, down 11.5% from the issue price of 32 rupees. The IPO was subscribed 4.93 times last week, a muted response for an IPO in recent months. Data from PRIME Database showed that about 66% of IPOs in the first half of fiscal year 2026-27 received more than 10 times the bids than were on offer. The company competes with Nykaa (FSNE.NS) and Meesho (MEES.NS) in India's growing e-commerce market. AceVector, which also owns Unicommerce and Stellaro Brands, posted a consolidated loss of 607.8 million Indian rupees for fiscal year 2026, with revenue of 5.1 billion rupees. "The valuation appears reasonable on a sales basis, but is not deeply attractive given the absence of profits," Swastika Investmart said in its note last week. AceVector's IPO comprised a fresh issue of shares worth 2.87 billion rupees and an offer for sale of up to 41.56 million shares by existing investors, including controlling shareholder Starfish, owned by SoftBank, and Nexus Venture Partners.
