item.title: NFL roundup: Cowboys' last-minute TD caps big 2nd half, upends Texans
item.description: Javonte Williams ran for three touchdowns in the second half and CeeDee Lamb scored on his 17th reception of the game with 40 seconds remaining as the Dallas Cowboys collected a high-voltage 34-30 comeback victory over the host Houston Texans on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Javonte Williams ran for three touchdowns in the second half and CeeDee Lamb scored on his 17th reception of the game with 40 seconds remaining as the Dallas Cowboys collected a high-voltage 34-30 comeback victory over the host Houston Texans on Sunday afternoon. Lamb posted a career-best 17 receptions and totaled 189 yards to help the Cowboys overcome a 10-point halftime deficit. Jason Witten (18 in 2012) is the only Dallas player to have more receptions in a game. Dak Prescott completed 32 of 45 passes for 335 yards and Williams had 62 yards on 19 carries for the Cowboys (2-2). C.J. Stroud was 21-of-31 passing for 347 yards and two touchdowns for the Texans (0-4), who have lost their first four games for the first time since 2020. Nico Collins caught seven passes for 118 yards and two scores after a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Woody Marks rushed for a score. Stroud guided the Texans on a nine-play, 87-yard drive to take a 30-27 lead with 2:23 left. The pivotal play was on third-and-14 from the Dallas 27-yard line. Stroud threw a short pass to Dalton Schultz at the 25. His lateral to David Montgomery was good for 19 more yards to the Cowboys' 6. Marks scored on the next play. Prescott then drove Dallas 74 yards on 11 plays, eventually connecting with Lamb for the winning points. Patriots 29, Bills 26 Drake Maye completed 22 of 37 passes for 269 yards and three touchdowns, including a late, go-ahead TD pass to Efton Chism III, to lead New England over Buffalo in Orchard Park, N.Y. Chism's leaping, one-handed 23-yard TD catch plus Maye's pass to Rhamondre Stevenson for the two-point conversion put the Patriots in front with 1:50 to play. Craig Woodson intercepted a Josh Allen pass at the New England 19-yard line on the ensuing possession, and the Patriots (2-2) were able to run out the clock and hand the Bills (3-1) their first loss in their new stadium. Allen was 23-of-33 passing for 253 yards and one touchdown. Buffalo's Keon Coleman caught six passes for 116 yards and a TD. James Cook rushed for 75 yards and a score. Ravens 24, Titans 18 Lamar Jackson threw for 222 yards and two touchdowns on 15-of-20 passing but exited early in Baltimore's home victory over Tennessee. Jackson was sacked on the Ravens' final play of the second quarter by Jermaine Johnson II, who landed on Jackson's left ankle. Jackson was later seen on the sideline with his ankle wrapped. Tyler Huntley played the second half and completed 8 of 9 passes for 63 yards, but the Ravens (3-1) were held scoreless after taking a 24-7 lead to the half. Cam Ward's 3-yard touchdown pass to Wan'Dale Robinson and two-point conversion pass to Gunnar Helm pulled the Titans (0-4) within six with 1:12 left. But Malaki Starks recovered Tennessee's ensuing onside kick with 1:10 left and Baltimore ran out the clock. Rams 24, Eagles 20 Kyren Williams rushed for two late touchdowns to rally Los Angeles over Philadelphia on a soggy afternoon in Philadelphia. Williams scored from 1 yard out with 3:59 left and from 7 yards out with 1:10 remaining to lift the Rams. Matthew Stafford overcame two first-half interceptions and finished with 317 yards on 32-of-51 passing for the Rams (2-2). Puka Nacua had a touchdown run to go with 125 yards on nine catches and Williams gained 147 yards (80 rushing, 67 receiving) from scrimmage. Byron Young sealed the win with two sacks on Philadelphia's final drive. Jalen Hurts threw two touchdowns to Darius Cooper and Philadelphia (2-2) built a 20-10 lead by halftime, but the offense largely struggled after losing Saquon Barkley to an early hamstring injury and finished 0-for-12 on third-down conversions with only 172 yards of offense. Hurts completed 12 of 27 passes for 93 yards. Jaguars 22, Bengals 17 Trevor Lawrence completed 18 of 23 passes for 227 yards and one touchdown to lead visiting Jacksonville past Cincinnati. It was the first time Lawrence defeated Joe Burrow in four career meetings. Bhayshul Tuten ran 17 times for 73 yards while Chris Rodriguez Jr. added a 25-yard touchdown run for the Jaguars (3-1). Burrow was 39-of-54 passing for 428 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions. Tee Higgins caught 11 passes for 157 yards while Chase Brown caught 11 passes for 71 yards for the Bengals (2-2), who played the second half without Ja'Marr Chase due to concussion symptoms. Bears 23, Jets 12 Kyle Monangai rushed for 146 yards and two touchdowns and Tyson Bagent passed for 268 yards to boost host Chicago to a victory against New York. Chicago (3-1) limited New York (1-3) to 157 total yards as the Jets lost their third game in a row. The Bears rolled up 492 yards of offense while collecting 34 first downs to the Jets' seven. Bagent finished 25-of-34 passing, Rome Odunze had six catches for 94 yards and Monangai finished with 30 carries. Geno Smith connected with Isaiah Williams for a 58-yard touchdown pass for New York, which enjoyed a rare bright spot when safety Minkah Fitzpatrick picked off Bagent in the second quarter. That stopped a record drought of 21 games without an interception for the Jets, who snagged their first pick since Jan. 5, 2025. Giants 36, Cardinals 24 Jameis Winston threw for 250 yards and three touchdowns as New York outlasted Arizona in East Rutherford, N.J. The Giants (3-1) shrugged off a 14-3 deficit as Winston fired second-quarter touchdown passes to Malachi Fields and Malik Nabers (six catches, 112 yards). Winston's 11-yard strike to Theo Johnson with 1:44 left in the third erased Arizona's last lead. Jacoby Brissett hit 21 of 35 passes for 166 yards, two yards and three interceptions. He drove the Cardinals (1-3) to the Giants' 2-yard line in the final minute trailing 30-24, but Deonte Banks picked off a fourth-down pass and returned it 98 yards for a score on the game's final play. Colts 30, Commanders 13 Jonathan Taylor ran for two touchdowns, and the Colts pulled away in the fourth quarter to beat the undermanned Commanders in London. Taylor finished with 95 yards and two touchdowns on 20 carries, as Indianapolis (2-2) made the most of their 257 yards. Quarterback Daniel Jones shrugged off a pair of early turnovers to complete 19 of 34 passes for 143 yards and an interception. Washington (1-3) played most of the day with rookie Athan Kaliakmanis at quarterback after starter Marcus Mariota suffered a right knee injury in the first quarter and wasn't able to return. Kaliakmanis completed 15 of 33 passes for 186 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Packers 17, Buccaneers 14 Jordan Love threw for 197 yards and two touchdowns as Green Bay held on against Tampa Bay in Tampa, Fla. Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft caught 2-yard touchdown passes from Love as the Packers (2-2) never trailed. Evan Williams and Edgerrin Cooper picked off passes and Trey Smack booted a 58-yard field goal to give Green Bay a 10-7 halftime lead. For Tampa Bay (0-4), rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels hit 19 of 27 passes for 148 yards and rushed for 55 yards in his first start playing for the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb). Sean Tucker rushed for a touchdown and Kenneth Gainwell caught a 10-yard touchdown pass to cut the Packers' lead to 17-14 with 14:49 to play. 49ers 24, Broncos 14 Deebo Samuel and Christian McCaffrey scored 1-yard touchdowns, George Kittle took a screen pass 56 yards for a clinching score and San Francisco remained unbeaten with a victory over Denver in Santa Clara, Calif. Eddy Pineiro contributed a 24-yard field goal and linebacker Dre Greenlaw, who played last season for the Broncos, led a strong San Francisco defensive effort with 12 tackles, helping the 49ers open the season with four consecutive wins for the second time in the past four years. Bo Nix went 25-for-42 for 214 yards, connecting 10 times with RJ Harvey for 68 yards for the Broncos (2-2). J.K. Dobbins had 40 of Denver's 82 rushing yards. Seahawks 30, Chargers 23 Emanuel Wilson scored two touchdowns and Seattle held off a late rally to defeat visiting Los Angeles. Wilson rushed 21 times for a game-high 81 yards and a touchdown and made three receptions for 39 yards and another score for the Seahawks (3-1), who held a 27-6 lead early in the third quarter. Sam Darnold was 13-of-22 passing for 168 yards and two scores for Seattle and Jaxon Smith-Njigba had five catches for 76 yards. Justin Herbert completed 19 of 31 passes for 189 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions for the Chargers (0-4), who committed four turnovers. The teams combined for 30 penalties, the most in an NFL game this season. Vikings 15, Dolphins 10 T.J. Hockenson had a career-high-tying 13 receptions and gained 119 yards and Minnesota improved to 4-0 for the 11th time in franchise history with the win over Miami in Minneapolis. Will Reichard matched his career best of five field goals and Kyler Murray completed 27 of 37 passes for 247 yards for the Vikings. Aaron Jones Sr. finished with 128 all-purpose yards (94 rushing, 34 receiving). Ollie Gordon II had nine carries for 100 yards and a touchdown to lead Miami (0-4). Malik Willis completed 9 of 17 passes for 85 yards and lost a fumble. Chiefs 30, Raiders 27 Patrick Mahomes, Kenneth Walker III and Kansas City planted their flag atop the AFC West with a 30-27 victory over host Las Vegas. Walker III had 22 carries for 177 yards and two touchdowns. Mahomes won his 99th regular-season game and threw two TD passes to wide receiver Tyquan Thornton, who exited with a leg injury. Wideout Rashee Rice also left the game with a first-quarter injury. The Chiefs (4-0) enter their bye week as the last undefeated team in the AFC. After Kansas City scored two fourth-quarter touchdowns in a 19-second span, Kirk Cousins (365 passing yards, two TDs) led a touchdown drive for the Raiders to cut the deficit to 30-27 with 1:46 left. Las Vegas' (3-1) would-be game-winning drive ended on his lone interception in the closing seconds. Panthers 32, Lions 26 Carolina's Bryce Young threw two touchdown passes to Tetairoa McMillan and the injury-riddled Panthers defense limited Detroit to two touchdowns in a win in Charlotte. Chuba Hubbard racked up 122 rushing yards and a pair of touchdowns on 20 carries for the Panthers (2-2). Young completed 29 of 41 passes for 329 yards. McMillan's 14 receptions accounted for 192 yards. Jared Goff was 32-for-52 passing for 412 yards and one touchdown for the Lions (2-2). Jameson Williams made six receptions for 102 yards. Jake Bates kicked field goals from 54, 43, 41 and 26 yards. --Field Level Media

item.title: Chiefs WRs Rashee Rice, Tyquan Thornton suffer injuries
item.description: Kansas City Chiefs wide receivers Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton were injured during Sunday's game at Las Vegas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kansas City Chiefs wide receivers Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton were injured during Sunday's game at Las Vegas. Rice suffered a hamstring injury after corralling a first-down pass from Patrick Mahomes in the right flat during the first quarter of the Chiefs' 30-27 win. Rice had room to run but limped toward the sideline and out of bounds at the Kansas City 36 after a five-yard gain. Rice remained on the sideline, stretching and chatting with Chiefs vice president of sports medicine and performance Rick Burkholder. He didn't return to the game. Thornton suffered a gruesome left ankle injury in the fourth quarter after reeling in a 55-yard pass from Mahomes. Treydan Stukes tackled Thornton from behind and the two got twisted as they fell to the ground. Thornton celebrated the catch by raising his right arm toward the stands. But he crumbled to the ground as soon as he tried to stand, and his left ankle was twisted in the other direction. "It doesn't look good," Chiefs coach Andy Reid said of Thornton's injury, adding he expects him to be back in Kansas City with the team. NFL Network reported later Sunday night that Thornton sustained a dislocated ankle that was put back in place by doctors and will be evaluated on Monday. He is out indefinitely, per the report. With the Chiefs' receiver depth taking a few hits, ESPN reported that Kansas City has remained in contact with former Chiefs wideout Tyreek Hill and his agent Drew Rosenhaus about a potential reunion. Hill, 32, was released by the Dolphins in February as a salary-cap-reduction measure after he sustained a dislocated left knee and tore ligaments in his knee last September, ending his season after just four games. Hill played his first six seasons in Kansas City from 2016-21, catching 479 passes for 6,630 yards and 56 touchdowns, earning six Pro Bowl nods and three first-team All-Pro honors. "It's almost time to get off the couch and get to work," Hill posted on his X account last week as he nears full health after an extensive recovery process. --Field Level Media

item.title: Oil slips as Middle East crude exports rise, G7 to release stocks
item.description: Brent crude futures climbed to $103.06 a barrel.
item.dc:creator: Florence Tan
item.content:encoded: Oil prices edged lower on Monday as rising Middle East crude exports and a release of oil stocks by the Group of Seven nations boosted supplies, offsetting concerns about further damage to Gulf oil infrastructure amid the US-Israeli war on Iran. Brent crude futures fell 66 cents, or 0.65%, to $101.59 a barrel at 0240 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $90.12 a barrel, down 95 cents, or 1.03%. Brent gave up most of its gains last week while WTI was 1.6% lower after [USN:L6N45O0G5 TEXT:"G7 countries"] agreed on Friday to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude from emergency reserves and pledged to refrain from energy export restrictions after pressure from US President Donald Trump. The release will add to [USN:L1N45R00B TEXT:"Middle Eastern crude exports"] which rose above pre-war levels in four of the seven days of the final week of September, shipping data showed on Monday, despite attacks on vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz. "The G7 decision to tap strategic reserves is taking some of the immediate supply anxiety out of the price, while there's a growing view that Saudi export volumes are moving back toward pre-war levels, even if those barrels are still moving at higher cost and via less efficient routes," said Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade. "That combination is enough to subdue prices for now even though the risks of further damage to energy infrastructure around the Gulf region haven't gone away." The Houthis said they [USN:S8N441065 TEXT:"launched"] ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and the Khurais area of Saudi Arabia in response to 50 Saudi-led air and missile strikes in Yemen in the past 12 hours. There was no confirmation from Saudi Arabia. On Sunday, Yemen's Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government said it was launching a major [USN:L1N45Q02D TEXT:"military campaign"] to recapture all areas of the country controlled by the Iran-backed Houthis. Meanwhile, Aramco has [USN:L1N45Q05Y TEXT:"unexpectedly cut"] November crude oil prices for Asia to six-year lows. Brent prices continue to stay above $100 per barrel on persistent geopolitical tensions and an increase in attacks on commercial vessels in the Gulf, ING analysts said in a note. Meanwhile, [USN:L6N45O0QD TEXT:"OPEC+ delayed"] a review that would determine 2027 oil output quotas for its members after the Iran war disrupted projects to expand capacity across the Middle East, throwing estimates of future production potential into uncertainty, said two sources close to the matter. In Europe, [USN:L1N45Q01Z TEXT:"Ukraine"] will double down on attacking Russian oil refineries, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy told Reuters in an interview published on Saturday.

item.title: Britain set to levy tariffs on Chinese electric cars, The Times reports
item.description: Britain is considering imposing tariffs on Chinese electric vehicle imports amid concerns that Beijing is flooding the market with state-subsidised cars, the Times newspaper reported on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Britain is considering imposing tariffs on Chinese electric vehicle imports amid concerns that Beijing is flooding the market with state-subsidised cars, the Times newspaper reported on Sunday. Business minister Jonathan Reynolds is drawing up a package of potential tariffs on Chinese vehicle imports, the report said, citing concerns that Chinese manufacturers are "dumping" subsidised vehicles into Britain. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Asked to comment, a spokesperson from the British government told Reuters no tariffs have been imposed on Chinese EVs. "We continue to engage closely with industry so that our approach reflects the sector’s and UK’s national interests," the spokesperson said in an email. British ministers are ready to match the European Union's 45% levy on Chinese electric cars, the Times said, to avoid the pain of "Made in Europe" proposals, which could impact UK companies selling into the EU. The EU's "[USN:L8N42K09E TEXT:"Made in Europe"]" policy is aimed at reducing reliance on Chinese components by prioritising European-made goods, raising concerns among British automakers that supply parts into European manufacturing chains and sell vehicles across the bloc. Burnham [USN:L8N45E0EA TEXT:"said"] last month he would make the case that Britain should be treated as a "trusted partner" under the proposed EU rules, warning that excluding the UK could damage its car industry. The Financial Times reported in September [USN:FWN45G1EO TEXT:"that Brussels had urged"] British Prime Minister Andy Burnham to align more closely with EU trade policy and raise tariffs on Chinese cars if Britain wants to avoid the "made in Europe" barriers. According to the Times, citing senior government sources, ministers believe any decision on tariffs should be based on Britain's national interest rather than automatically following the EU's lead.

item.title: US removes B-1 bombers from UK base amid security concerns
item.description: The United States removed its B-1 bombers from a UK air base one week after several men were arrested there on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts, a Pentagon official said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Svea Herbst-Bayliss
item.content:encoded: The United States removed its B-1 bombers from a UK air base one week after several men were arrested there on suspicion of preparing terrorist acts, a Pentagon official said on Sunday. A dozen B-1 bombers were stationed at RAF Fairford air base, located northwest of London. The planes had been used for US strikes on Iran. "While operational security precluded us from confirming the movement of our assets and forces in real-time, we can acknowledge now that all US bombers that were deployed to RAF Fairford have re-deployed to their home stations in the United States," a Pentagon spokesman wrote in an email. Britain has "strong indications" that [USN:L1N45M0MW TEXT:"Iran was involved"] in a [USN:L1N45O076 TEXT:"suspected plot"] targeting the base, Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Wednesday. Iran said accusations linking Tehran to the alleged plan were baseless and summoned the British ambassador in Tehran over the issue. The Wall Street Journal first reported that the aircraft were removed from the base amid security concerns over suspected terror plots against the facility. The British government had allowed the US to use bombers based at Fairford to strike Iranian missile sites that were attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz. US President [USN:L8N45K0CX TEXT:"Donald Trump said those involved in the plot"] had planned "big damage" while US Secretary of State Marco Rubio also pointed to the "hands of a foreign actor."

item.title: Cowboys stun Texans 34-30 behind CeeDee Lamb, huge second half
item.description: Javonte Williams ran for three touchdowns in the second half and CeeDee Lamb scored on his 17th reception of the game with 40 seconds remaining as the Dallas Cowboys collected a high-voltage 34-30 comeback victory over the host Houston Texans on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Javonte Williams ran for three touchdowns in the second half and CeeDee Lamb scored on his 17th reception of the game with 40 seconds remaining as the Dallas Cowboys collected a high-voltage 34-30 comeback victory over the host Houston Texans on Sunday afternoon. Lamb posted a career-best 17 receptions and totaled 189 yards to help Dallas overcome a 10-point halftime deficit. Jason Witten (18 in 2012) is the only Dallas player to have more receptions in a game. Dak Prescott completed 32 of 45 passes for 335 yards and Williams had 62 yards on 19 carries for the Cowboys (2-2). C.J. Stroud was 21-of-31 passing for 347 yards and two touchdowns for the Texans (0-4), who have lost their first four games for the first time since 2020. Houston's Nico Collins caught seven passes for 118 yards and two scores after a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Woody Marks rushed for a score. Stroud guided the Texans on a nine-play, 87-yard drive to take a 30-27 lead with 2:23 left. The pivotal play was on third-and-14 from the Dallas 27-yard line. Stroud threw a short pass to tight end Dalton Schultz at the 25. His lateral to David Montgomery was good for 19 more yards to the Cowboys' 6. Marks scored on the next play. Prescott then drove Dallas 74 yards on 11 plays, eventually connecting with Lamb for the winning points. Dallas trailed by 10 at the break but KaVontae Turpin opened the third quarter with a 48-yard kickoff return to the Texans' 49. Four plays later, Williams scored on an 8-yard run to bring the Cowboys 16-13. Houston answered with its own impressive kickoff return as Jaylin Noel went 53 yards to the Dallas 38. Four plays later, Stroud tossed a 22-yard touchdown pass to Collins to give the Texans a 23-13 advantage with 10:50 left in the quarter. Later in the quarter, Williams scored from the 1 as Dallas pulled within three with 6:49 left. On their next possession, the Cowboys drove 81 yards on 14 plays with Williams scoring on a 2-yard run to give Dallas its first lead at 27-23 with 11:17 left in the game. Stroud threw a touchdown pass to Collins and Ka'imi Fairbairn kicked three field goals as the Texans led 16-6 at halftime. Houston took the opening kickoff and went 85 yards on eight plays. Stroud hit Collins for 45 yards at the outset of the drive and later connected on a 7-yard scoring pass to Collins. Dallas responded with Brandon Aubrey's 39-yard field goal with 5:10 left before Fairbairn was good from 51 yards to give the Texans a 10-3 advantage with 1:49 remaining. Aubrey drilled a 50-yard field goal to bring the Cowboys within 10-6 with 12:30 left in the half. Fairbairn added field goals of 39 and 54. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jameis Winston, Giants outlast Cardinals to move to 3-1
item.description: Jameis Winston tossed three touchdown passes and the New York Giants outlasted the Arizona Cardinals 36-24 on Sunday in East Rutherford, N.J.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jameis Winston tossed three touchdown passes and the New York Giants outlasted the Arizona Cardinals 36-24 on Sunday in East Rutherford, N.J. Winston overcame two interceptions and four sacks to complete 18 of 29 passes for 250 yards. He found tight end Theo Johnson on an 11-yard connection late in the third quarter for the go-ahead score. In a back-and-forth game with three lead changes and six turnovers, the Giants (3-1) had to climb out of a 14-3 first-quarter hole. New York turned things around with Winston's touchdown passes to Malachi Fields and Malik Nabers in the final 4:30 of the first half, which followed the second of three Dominic Zvada field goals. The Giants' halftime lead was cut to 19-17 when the Cardinals' Chad Ryland booted a 60-yard field goal as time expired. The Cardinals reclaimed the lead midway through the third quarter when Jacoby Brissett found a wide-open Elijah Higgins over the middle for a 2-yard touchdown pass to make it 24-19. But they couldn't come up with any more points as they ventured into Giants territory just once in their final four possessions. Arizona (1-3) lost its third straight game after a season-opening road win over the Los Angeles Chargers. Brissett completed 21 of 35 passes for 166 yards with two touchdowns and three interceptions, including a pick-6 on the game's final play. Giants running back Cam Skattebo ran for a key first down with just over three minutes left to allow New York to take more time off the clock, but the Giants settled for a 52-yard field goal by Zvada with 2:11 to play. The Cardinals had one more chance. Deonte Banks was whistled for an 18-yard pass interference call on a pass intended for Marvin Harrison Jr., which moved the Cardinals down to the Giants' 4-yard line with 22 seconds to play. After Brissett threw three straight incomplete passes, Banks redeemed himself on fourth down by intercepting Brissett and returning it 98 yards for a touchdown as the clock ran out. The Cardinals lost starting offensive tackle Paris Johnson Jr. to injury on the final drive. Earlier in the game, right guard Isaiah Adams and safety Andrew Wingard (knee) were carted off. --Field Level Media

item.title: France's Schneider Electric confirms $22.6 billion deal to buy US software firm PTC
item.description: France's Schneider Electric said on Monday it had agreed to buy PTC in an all-cash deal valuing the US software company's equity at around $22.6 billion, confirming reports from Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Sabrina Valle
item.content:encoded: France's Schneider Electric (SCHN.PA) said on Monday it had agreed to buy PTC (PTC.O) in an all-cash deal valuing the US software company's equity at around $22.6 billion, confirming reports from Sunday. The $205-per-share offer implies an enterprise value of $23.7 billion for Boston-based PTC and represents a 42.3% premium to its last closing share price. The deal will be financed through a combination of equity and new debt issuance and is expected to be closed in the third quarter of 2027. The acquisition would deepen the French engineering company's push into software acquisitions, having agreed to buy [USN:L6N432112 TEXT:"Cognite Holding"], a privately held provider of AI software and industrial data, in June. Schneider, once known primarily for industrial components like fuses and circuit breakers, now builds the backbone of data centres, supplying everything from cooling units and server racks to critical power distribution equipment. The booming demand for data centres, particularly from the United States, is driving [USN:L6N41D0F0 TEXT:"Schneider's earnings"], offering a growing source of revenue helping offset weakness in some traditional electrical-equipment markets. PTC, which provides software solutions for designing, manufacturing and servicing products across multiple sectors, has also [USN:L4N43V2I2 TEXT:"benefited"] from growing demand for its AI-powered tools. In July, Schneider Electric lifted its [USN:L4N43V2I2 TEXT:"annual revenue forecast"] after reporting record first-half results, betting on strong demand for its core industrial software and artificial intelligence-powered tools.

item.title: Yemeni government launches offensive to seize all areas from Iran-backed Houthis
item.description: Despite the preparations for a counteroffensive, the Houthis have maintained the initiative on the ground, weeks after seizing the Bab el-Mandeb Strait in a lightning offensive that saw government forces collapse.
item.dc:creator: Mohammed Ghobari, Timour Azhari, Eman Abouhassira
item.content:encoded: Yemen’s Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government said on Sunday it was launching a major military campaign to recapture all areas of the country controlled by the Iran-backed Houthis . The government’s armed forces would press the offensive “until the country is liberated from the grip of the terrorist militia,” Yemeni President Rashad al-Alimi said in a televised address. A military spokesman later called on the Houthis to lay down their weapons. The Houthis, known formally as Ansar Allah, have held Yemen’s capital Sanaa and vast parts of the northwest, where most of the population live, since 2014. They have so far withstood a series of attacks over the years by Saudi Arabia, the UAE and their Western allies, and have updated their weaponry with the help of Iran. The movement launched a surprise offensive last month which captured the strategic Bab el-Mandeb strait and some 150 km (90 miles) of coast on the Red Sea in a matter of weeks, giving the Houthis new leverage over the international shipping route. That advance also opened a new front in the wider US-Israeli war launched in February against Iran, to which Tehran’s responses included choking oil shipping through the Strait of Hormuz , to the other side of the Arabian Peninsula. HOUTHIS SAY THEY STRUCK SAUDI ARABIA As the Yemeni government, known as the Presidential Leadership Council, made its announcement, the Houthis said they had launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and the Khurais area of Saudi Arabia. They claimed the attacks caused major fires and were in response to what they said were 50 Saudi-led air and missile strikes in Yemen in the past 12 hours. There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia. Alimi said the decision to launch the counteroffensive came after all chances of de-escalating the conflict had been exhausted. He thanked Saudi Arabia for its support and called on Yemen's regional allies and international partners to support PLC forces and institutions. Regional and western officials had told Reuters earlier this week that Saudi Arabia and its Yemeni allies were planning to [USN:L8N45M1W0 TEXT:"launch an assault"] on the Houthis, with the Saudis leading aerial combat and Yemeni forces fighting on the ground. NEW FRONT IN MIDEAST WAR The US is already providing intelligence to support Riyadh's operations in Yemen, while some regional and European nations are providing mainly defensive military aid to the kingdom, six people with knowledge of the Saudi preparations told Reuters. The United States’ war on Iran has decimated a layer of Iranian military and political leadership, but has also entangled Washington in a new engagement in the Middle East and depleted crucial military hardware. Yemen has been mired in conflict for years, with an array of local armed groups and factions backed by competing regional and international actors. After a popular uprising that was part of the Arab Spring movements in 2011, the Houthis, an armed group of Zaidi Shi’ite Muslims, captured Sanaa. The Saudi-backed PLC, which is also recognised by the United Nations, has since the Houthi takeover controlled the south and east of the country, based in the former South Yemen capital of Aden. Saudi Arabia entered Yemen's civil war in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition in support of the PLC, but failed to defeat the Houthis. A truce agreed between the warring parties in 2022 largely held until this year, when the Houthis launched missile and drone attacks on Saudi shipping and oil infrastructure in a spillover from the Iran war. HOUTHIS ON FRONT FOOT The Houthis have maintained the initiative on the ground since seizing control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait in their lightning offensive last month that saw government forces collapse. Bab el-Mandeb is the southern exit passage of the Red Sea, a key shipping route between the Mediterranean and Asia that has assumed even more importance this year as an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz. In the last 48 hours, the Houthis have also made gains against government and local forces on strategic hilltops near Yemen's Taiz, military sources said, advancing on the last road between the city and Aden on the southern coast. Houthi control over the Taiz-Aden road would lead to an effective siege of the city, Yemen's third-largest, inhabited by hundreds of thousands of civilians and where thousands of government forces are also stationed. The city is important not just for its strategic location; Alimi is from the region, and a siege of Taiz would amplify an already-dire humanitarian situation in the country. Three in four families in parts of Yemen are going hungry from the impact of the surge in fighting, which has displaced tens of thousands of people and disrupted supplies to millions, the World Food Programme said last week.

item.title: Saudi Arabia to cancel Joy Awards, its answer to the Grammys, amid budget cuts, sources say
item.description: Saudi Arabia is set to cancel next year's Joy Awards, its star-studded answer to the Oscars or the Grammys, as financial strain and the Iran war hit the country's nascent entertainment sector, two people with knowledge of the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia is set to cancel next year's Joy Awards, its star-studded answer to the Oscars or the Grammys, as financial strain and the Iran war hit the country's nascent entertainment sector, two people with knowledge of the matter said. Held in January, the event has become the crown jewel of Riyadh's annual events calendar, drawing performers including Katy Perry and Robbie Williams this year and handing out awards in music as well as other areas of entertainment and sport. It is the latest high-profile entertainment event to face cancellation or postponement as Riyadh reprioritizes spending and cuts culture and entertainment budgets. A spokesperson for the General Entertainment Authority, which organizes the Joy Awards along with Saudi media conglomerate MBC Group, did not respond to a request for comment. MBC Group and the Saudi government's media office also did not respond to requests for comment. Industry sources say budget cuts were already felt before the Iran war, which has undermined Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's efforts to turn the kingdom into a destination for tourism and global events under his ambitious Vision 2030 plan. Flagship projects scaled back or indefinitely postponed over the last year or so include the 100-mile (161 km) steel and glass tower The Line at megacity NEOM, and a $50 billion steel and metal [USN:L1N3YR0WK TEXT:"cube"] in Riyadh. The government has also withdrawn funding from ventures such as LIV Golf, after spending over $5 billion on the startup, and is now quietly shelving plans to [USN:L6N45E0H2 TEXT:"build"] the NEOM Stadium, one of the main projects for the 2034 FIFA World Cup, two sources familiar with the matter said. "The war and its wider ripple effects are inevitably prompting Gulf states to reassess spending priorities," said Mazen Hayek, a Dubai-based media consultant. "It's not simply a question of whether governments have the financial capacity to fund such initiatives. Some of these events were also conceived as instruments of international visibility, soft power and influence. In the current environment, however, governments may be weighing those objectives against other national priorities," he said. FILM FESTIVAL, DESERT RAVE ALSO CANCELLED Last month, the Red Sea Film Festival was postponed until 2027, with organizers citing logistical constraints and other factors. Uncertainty over the Iran war has also made it difficult to book international stars for such events, the industry sources said. The Red Sea Film Festival was launched in 2021 as part of an effort to develop local cinema after Saudi Arabia lifted a decades-long ban on cinemas. Last month, organizers also called off Soundstorm, a city-sized rave in the desert due to be held in December that welcomes hundreds of thousands of partygoers and was headlined by Cardi B last year. Organizers said it would return next year, giving no reason for the cancellation. Soundstorm, also known as MDLBEAST, began in 2019 as new events were staged amid rapid social change under the crown prince, widely known as MbS, whose reforms sought to rein in the power of religious conservatives. With gender-mixing, dancing and displays of queer culture, the festival often drew the ire of religious conservatives and stunned even some of those who support other aspects of the kingdom's social opening. Events aimed at driving investment into the kingdom, such as the flagship Future Investment Initiative (FII) taking place at the end of this month, remain scheduled as planned, according to organizers. "Events that are important for the Saudi economy and showing its place in the world are still being prioritised; what isn't is anything that is singing and dancing and having a good time," a person working in the Saudi events industry said.

item.title: Australia probes flydubai co-pilot's links to the country, police say
item.description: The co-pilot, identified as an Omani, studied at a university in Melbourne, sources said.
item.dc:creator: Praveen Menon, Alexander Cornwell
item.content:encoded: A multi-agency Australian counterterrorism unit is investigating links to Australia of the co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073, who stabbed his captain and then [USN:L1N45P01E TEXT:"attempted to hijack"] the plane, a police spokesperson said on Sunday. The Victorian Joint Counter Terrorism Team – which comprises federal police, Victorian state police and the ASIO intelligence agency – was "investigating the man's links to Australia," the Australian Federal Police spokesperson said. Two sources briefed on the investigation said the co-pilot studied at a university in Melbourne, the capital of the Australian state of Victoria, without identifying which one. A third source said he studied at RMIT University in Melbourne around a decade ago. In a brief statement on Monday, RMIT confirmed that the co-pilot had been enrolled at the university but he did not successfully complete an engineering qualification. RMIT did not name the co-pilot or say when he studied there. The co-pilot of the [USN:L1N45P02M TEXT:"flydubai flight FZ1073"], which was bound for Israel from Dubai on Wednesday, attacked the pilot with an emergency crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general said on Saturday, calling the incident a "[USN:S8N43T02Z TEXT:"terrorist attack"]". Flight FZ1073 would have felt like a [USN:L4N45Q00M TEXT:""vertical roller coaster""], when it plunged 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds before being levelled out and landing safely, according to an aviation instructor who recreated the descent in a flight simulator for Reuters. CO-PILOT IN CUSTODY IN UAE Two sources have said the co-pilot is an Omani national named Hamam Al-Hammami. Israeli officials have not named the co-pilot but said that he is from Oman. UAE authorities and flydubai have not publicly disclosed the co-pilot's identity. Reuters could not independently reach Al-Hammami, who is in UAE custody, for comment. The UAE has not announced any formal charges against him and it is not known if he has appointed legal counsel. Oman has not commented on the incident. Disaster on board flight FZ1073 was averted after passengers and crew subdued the co-pilot, who had attacked the captain in what Israeli officials said was an attempt to crash the plane carrying more than 170 passengers and crew. The UAE public prosecutor has said the co-pilot had attempted to take control of the plane. RADICAL MOSQUES AND EXTREMIST WEBSITES Most of the passengers on board were Israeli nationals. A reserve flydubai pilot travelling on the flight took control of the aircraft and landed it at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia, where the co-pilot was detained by Saudi authorities and later transferred to the UAE on Thursday. The Financial Times reported on Sunday that Al-Hamami had allegedly visited what it described as radical mosques and extremist websites while in Australia, citing two people familiar with the investigation. Australian intelligence services held a file on the individual, according to the Financial Times. Reuters could not immediately verify the FT report. The government of Australia did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside normal business hours. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the co-pilot had undergone radical [USN:L6N45N0GW TEXT:"Islamist indoctrination"] and was clearly suicidal, although he has not said when or where that indoctrination allegedly occurred. On Sunday he instructed the National Security Council to appoint an examiner to "conduct a thorough review of all security aspects regarding foreign civil aviation to Israel". Israel does not have official diplomatic relations with Oman, and Netanyahu has also said pilots from such countries were not permitted to operate flights to Israel. It is not clear how the co-pilot came to be assigned to the flight to Tel Aviv.

item.title: Bolsonaro will face Lula in runoff in Brazil's presidential vote
item.description: Right-wing Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro will face leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in a runoff of the presidential election later this month, after he exceeded expectations in Sunday's first-round vote with a slight lead over the incumbent.
item.dc:creator: Luciana Magalhaes, Lisandra Paraguassu, Ricardo Brito, Brendan O'Boyle
item.content:encoded: Right-wing Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro will face leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in a runoff of the presidential election later this month, after he exceeded expectations in Sunday's first-round vote with a slight lead over the incumbent. The election, which centered around the [USN:L6N459162 TEXT:"cost of living"], corruption and insecurity in Brazilians' daily lives, follows a string of wins across Latin America by right-wing parties aligned with US President Donald Trump. Bolsonaro's stronger-than-expected performance, at 47% of votes versus Lula's 45%, is expected to buoy his campaign and may bolster Brazil's currency and stock market, which have risen on the prospects of the business-friendly challenger. Private surveys in the run-up to the election had forecast Lula leading the first-round vote by around 3 percentage points. "Brazil wants change and I am very happy with the results," Bolsonaro told reporters in Brasilia after nearly all tallies were reported, heralding "the end of the era of (Lula's) Workers' Party." The senator, son of [USN:L1N45F0NC TEXT:"right-wing former President"] Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year [USN:S0N3UJ08N TEXT:"sentence"] for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election, now heads to an October 25 showdown with the [USN:L1N45G04J TEXT:"leftist Lula"]. Addressing a crowd at a hotel in Sao Paulo, Lula said he had been convinced he would win the election in the first round. "Starting tomorrow, we begin a new campaign," he said, promising to show voters what he had accomplished as president. Despite growing worries over Brazil's public finances and sluggish economic growth, the campaign offered [USN:L1N4580UE TEXT:"meager policy debate"], as both leading candidates skipped the major TV debates. SURPRISE SHOWING "The pollsters missed badly," said Robert Muggah, cofounder of think-tank Igarape Institute. "Expect the runoff polls, which show a dead heat, to understate Bolsonaro as well." Early on Sunday, Bolsonaro told journalists in Rio de Janeiro he was counting on "a protest vote from people who would otherwise vote for another candidate but are opposed to Lula." Thaise Lima, a 41-year-old lawyer on her way to vote in Sao Paulo, said her main goal was to get Lula's Workers' Party out of office. "I don't think Flavio is the best candidate, but I might decide to vote for him in the next few minutes," she said, adding that she wished psychiatrist and author Augusto Cury were a more viable candidate. Fernando Tempel, 49, a management consultant, told Reuters he was voting for Bolsonaro despite initially planning to vote for Romeu Zema, the former governor of Minas Gerais state. "The protest vote foreshadows what is to come in the runoff," said political analyst Rafael Favetti. "While this should benefit Flavio Bolsonaro now, his growth potential in the second round drops precisely because that support has already been front-loaded." ECONOMIC HEADWINDS Despite Brazil's [USN:L1N44111S TEXT:"falling inequality"] and unemployment, Lula has struggled to win over voters grappling with the high cost of living, heavy household debt and the threat of crime and more pervasive gang activity. Bolsonaro has sought to capitalize on cost-of-living concerns, while Lula moved to ban online gambling and, as the race tightened, expanded welfare and proposed fresh debt relief for families. Rising spending and public debt above 82% of GDP have stoked fiscal concerns that Brazil's next president will need to address. The government lowered its [USN:L1N45E0QC TEXT:"economic growth forecasts"] for this year and next to 2.0% and 2.3%, respectively. "I voted for Brazil to start growing again," said Marciano de Souza e Silva, a 52-year-old public servant in Brasilia who voted for Flavio. OVERSHADOWED DEBATE Scandals and fears of foreign interference ahead of the vote largely overshadowed policy debates during the campaign. Controversy surrounding the now-defunct Banco Master engulfed much of Brazil's political class after Daniel Vorcaro, who ran the bank, was arrested earlier this year and accused of a multibillion-dollar fraud scheme, which he denies. A federal police investigation has looked into the banker's ties to figures across Brazil's political elite, including Bolsonaro, who is being [USN:L1N4530BQ TEXT:"investigated for "][USN:L1N4530BQ TEXT:"suspected money "][USN:L1N4530BQ TEXT:"laundering"] that police have tied to the case. Bolsonaro has denied wrongdoing. Throughout the campaign, Lula's allies have warned that the Trump administration might refuse to recognize election results if he wins, pointing to an aborted effort to [USN:L6N43R03C TEXT:"send US officials to Brazil"]. Trump has not formally endorsed a candidate, though he hosted Senator Bolsonaro at the White House and praised him publicly. Reuters reported on Wednesday that Brazilian intelligence officials briefed a French and German delegation on [USN:L1N45E08V TEXT:"alleged US and Russian interference"] before the election. The US has rejected claims of interference in Brazil's affairs. On Sunday afternoon, Brazil's electoral court chief Kassio Nunes Marques said the election was running smoothly.

item.title: Like a 'vertical roller coaster': Simulating flight FZ1073's sudden plunge
item.description: A prolonged high-speed dive can place extreme strain on an airframe, an expert says.
item.dc:creator: Ben Makori
item.content:encoded: Flydubai's [USN:S8N44D013 TEXT:"flight FZ1073"], which plunged 16,000 feet in about 30 seconds before being levelled out and landing safely, would have felt like a "vertical roller coaster", according to an aviation instructor who recreated the descent in a flight simulator for Reuters. The steep fall, after an attack on the captain by the co-pilot during a flight on Wednesday, would have put huge strain on the Boeing 737 MAX 8 aircraft - as well as the passengers and crew, said Alberto Paduanelli, owner of ALPA Simulation in Sherfield on Loddon, southern England. The co-pilot of the flydubai jet, which was bound for Israel from Dubai, attacked the pilot with an emergency crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general said on Saturday, calling the incident a "[USN:L1N45P01E TEXT:"terrorist attack"]". The co-pilot was identified as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national, two sources with knowledge of the investigation told Reuters. UAE authorities did not immediately respond to a request for confirmation of his identity. Reuters could not independently reach al-Hammami for comment. Flydubai says the circumstances surrounding the incident are still under investigation and it cannot comment further. Oman has yet to comment on the incident. "A plunge of 16,000 feet (4,877 metres) over 30 seconds will feel like you are over on a very, very vertical roller coaster," Paduanelli said, sitting at the controls of the simulator cockpit. "The difference is that on the roller coaster, you know what's happening," he said, adding that with a sudden drop "you feel the negative g-force on your body". For passengers who are not strapped in, "Your body will literally lift from the seat", he said. Using a simulator to recreate the incident, Paduanelli said the aircraft's autopilot disconnected before the plunge began, causing the jet to accelerate rapidly. US President Donald Trump has praised the Boeing jet for withstanding the severe forces put on it during the incident. The plane was levelled out after passengers overpowered the co-pilot, before a reserve crew of pilots onboard landed the plane. "It was an amazing show of precise and powerful structural planning and design," Trump posted on Truth Social, adding that the 737 Max "was able to withstand G Forces and Strain far beyond what it was designed and expected to do". Boeing did not respond to a request for comment. Aircraft are designed and tested to withstand substantial aerodynamic loads, but Paduanelli said a prolonged high-speed dive can place extreme strain on an airframe. "This was nothing but a miracle that nothing was hurt apart from the captain, unfortunately, and that two pilots were onboard," Paduanelli said. Details about al-Hammami's past have trickled out. Royal Air Maroc told Reuters he did a three-month training with the airline in 2025 but his application to work there afterwards was rejected. Buckinghamshire New University in Britain said he did a distance-learning course in aviation management with the institution, but no pilot training. An Australian Federal Police spokesperson said on Sunday that authorities there were investigating al-Hammami's "links to Australia". A source briefed on the investigation said the co-pilot studied at a university in Melbourne.

item.title: Saudi Arabia quietly shelving NEOM Stadium, one of 2034 World Cup venues
item.description: It was meant to be one of the most ambitious venues for the 2034 FIFA World Cup.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari, Federico Maccioni
item.content:encoded: Saudi Arabia is quietly shelving plans to build one of its most ambitious stadiums for the 2034 FIFA World Cup, two sources familiar with the matter said, after delays and downscaling of the futuristic development housing it. The NEOM Stadium was billed as an elevated arena in a glitzy 100-mile (160-km) steel and glass structure known as The Line, in turn part of the broader development known as NEOM. NEOM was introduced about a decade ago as a centrepiece of de facto ruler Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's Vision 2030, an ambitious plan to diversify the economy and cut reliance on oil. Yasir Al-Rumayyan, governor of NEOM's owner the Public Investment Fund, confirmed in April that The Line was [USN:S8N40J01E TEXT:"no longer a priority"], and said it was not vital before 2030, the original delivery target for its first phase. He denied any projects had been cancelled. However, according to two sources, plans to build the NEOM Stadium have now been shelved indefinitely. NEOM and the Saudi government media office did not reply to requests for comment, while Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Sports redirected questions to the World Cup 2034 Hosting Higher Authority. The Authority said "substantial delivery" of construction milestones for the event was already taking place, but did not address questions around the NEOM Stadium and costs. It shared images of some of the other stadiums under construction. RIYADH DEVELOPING 15 VENUES FOR 2034 WORLD CUP The 2034 World Cup is seen as a marquee event for Saudi Arabia, which under the Vision 2030 programme has invested heavily in sports via wealth fund PIF. The tournament will be the first time a single nation hosts the expanded 48-team format. Riyadh is working to build or renovate 15 venues across five cities, as well as dozens of training facilities. MEED Projects, a Dubai-based construction industry market intelligence platform whose team of analysts tracks tenders and projects in the region, puts the total value of the projects at $22.7 billion in data shared with Reuters. According to MEED, NEOM's stadium is expected to cost $2.5 billion. It lists the projected 46,000-seat stadium in its data as "on hold". The stadium has no listed completion date, according to the data, which describes the remaining stadiums and facilities as in various stages of development, with completion expected between 2026 and 2033. Saudi Arabia is under increasing pressure from the Iran war, which has led to heavy disruptions to energy shipments and damage to critical infrastructure, with the kingdom facing attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis. Last week, the Ministry of Finance said it [USN:L1N45M0WE TEXT:"expected"] a fiscal deficit this year wider than previously projected and a real GDP contraction of 3.6% following a drop in oil activities. PIVOT FROM GIGA-PROJECTS The geographic distribution of the stadiums adds to the challenge of delivering the projects, a third source said. That could further be compounded by some projects set to host stadiums being delayed or downsized, such as The Line or Riyadh's New Murabba development, the source added. In January Reuters [USN:L1N3YR0WK TEXT:"reported"] that Saudi Arabia has suspended construction of The Mukaab, a colossal cube-shaped skyscraper at the centre of the New Murabba. Reuters also reported last year that the PIF was pivoting from its focus on costly giga-projects to endeavours with more immediate financial returns, a strategy [USN:L1N40Y0DC TEXT:"later articulated"] by Saudi officials. Still, other projects for the World Cup are progressing. The [USN:L6N43I0ZY TEXT:"Aramco Stadium"] in the eastern city of Al Khobar is set to be completed by the end of this year and host its first game in January, for which tickets are on sale. Work on other planned stadiums is going ahead, a fourth source said.

item.title: Revolut's rise to become Europe's $115 billion big bank rival
item.description: Revolut has become Europe's most valuable startup and a challenge to centuries-old banking giants, though it faces hurdles.
item.dc:creator: Lawrence White, Elizabeth Howcroft
item.content:encoded: Revolut has risen to become Europe's most valuable startup and a challenge to centuries-old banking giants, having grown rapidly since it was launched just over a decade ago as a fintech promising cheaper forex fees. Yet Revolut faces many hurdles itself, with the amount of revenue it extracts per customer a fraction of its established competitors and a small lending business by industry standards. A spokesperson for Revolut said in an email that the London-based company has a "diversified business model", earning its revenue from various products and services rather than lending. "That means our growth depends on building things customers value, rather than on interest rates," the spokesperson said. Here's Revolut's rise, in five charts: GOING FOR GLOBAL CEO Nik Storonsky has stressed he wants Revolut to be truly global, expanding into markets [USN:L4N44E0AO TEXT:"from Mexico to Australia"]. The company has announced several new licences in recent weeks, as it aims to become one of only a handful of banks with retail operations spanning so much of the globe. Meanwhile, some traditional lenders seen as global, including HSBC (HSBA.L) , are reducing their retail footprint. Valued at $115 billion privately, Revolut is now worth more than Britain's Barclays (BARC.L) and France's Societe Generale (SOGN.PA) as investors bet on its tech platform winning over more customers globally. Revolut's 2025 pretax profit was £1.7 billion ($2.2 billion), a fraction of Barclays' £9 billion, but growing fast. Paulo Macedo, CEO of Portugal's biggest bank, Caixa Geral de Depósitos, said in June that 2025 was the last year in which the 150-year-old bank would record higher profit than Revolut. "When you go to Europe the bank CEOs there are talking about Revolut as their most important threat because of their aggressive marketing and growth," said Cihan Duran, director at S&P Global Ratings. MARRED BY SETBACKS In the US, where Revolut has a provisional license, it will face tougher competition, investors said. "The US could be potentially the biggest growth for Revolut. But at the same time, the US is the most competitive market," said Konstantin Sidorov, CEO of the London Technology Club, which invested in Revolut when it was valued at just $5.5 billion. There have been setbacks, including a fine in Lithuania for failing to prevent money laundering. Revolut said an investigation had not identified any confirmed instances of money laundering, adding that it had signed a settlement with the central bank and taken steps to resolve shortcomings. And in September, Revolut accidentally sent customer data to hackers posing as government investigators. The company said its systems and customer funds were unaffected and it had contacted the "limited number of impacted individuals" to give support. In 2024 and 2025, Revolut was the most-complained-about bank in Britain in fraud cases whereby customers are tricked into sending cash to scammers, Ombudsman data compiled by consumer advocacy firm Which? showed. Revolut has previously said in response it takes fraud very seriously and has robust customer protections in place. CUSTOMERS HAVE SURGED A striking measure of its growth is customer numbers. In Ireland, for example, Revolut said that 80% of the adult population has a Revolut account. Revolut's website shows it has 80 million customers, against 84 million for JPMorgan (JPM.N) and 41 million for HSBC. REVENUE-PER-CUSTOMER IS LOW Revolut makes far less from each of its customers than traditional banks, a Reuters analysis of its figures shows. Average deposit balances are also much lower. Lower per-customer revenue is in part because Revolut lends much less than traditional banks, instead relying on fees such as card subscriptions. With just £2.2 billion in loans at end-2025, Revolut's loan-to-deposit ratio of 6% compares with 55% for HSBC and 86% for Societe Generale. Scaling its lending business will introduce risks including managing big and complex credit exposures, while entering fiercely competitive local mortgage markets will not be easy, analysts and investors said. TOO FEW PRIMARY ACCOUNTS Revolut has attracted customers with its easy-to-use app but executives acknowledge too few use it as a primary bank account. Revolut declined to comment in its latest results on how many customers did so in 2025, but said the figure was up 45% from a year ago. This metric is a focus for Revolut's biggest backers. Alex Immerman, an investor at Andreessen Horowitz, which is known as "a16z", told Reuters it was watching for primary-account adoption, as well as total customer balances. ($1 = 0.7573 pounds)

item.title: Leftist, nationalists set to win election for Bosnia's tripartite presidency
item.description: Voters are casting ballots for the central tripartite presidency and national parliament.
item.dc:creator: Branko Filipovic, Fedja Grulovic
item.content:encoded: A Bosniak left-leaning moderate, a pro-Russian Serb nationalist and a Croatian nationalist are leading Sunday's election for Bosnia's inter-ethnic tripartite presidency, the election commission said early on Monday, based on ballots from 96.31% of polling stations. The results were largely in line with expectations and with projections by the Poliwave tracking platform, although voter turnout was low at a combined 42.02% in Bosnia's two entities, the Bosniak-Croat Federation and the Serb Republika Srpska. Voters also cast ballots for the national parliament, alongside regional races in the two entities. Voter frustration has grown over an economic slowdown, the slow pace of EU entry talks and a lingering political crisis in which ethnically based dominant parties from the two entities have repeatedly stalled decisions by the weak central government that links them. Denis Becirovic, a Bosniak of the Social Democratic Party (SDP-BiH) and part of the current tripartite presidency, garnered 26.78% of votes in the Bosniak-Croat Federation, ahead of the candidate for the centre-right Muslim Party of Democratic Action (SDA). The two had been considered favourites in the election. Also leading in the Bosniak-Croat Federation was newcomer Darijana Filipovic of the nationalist and pro-European Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ-BiH), with 13.89% of the vote. In Republika Srpska, Zeljka Cvijanovic, an existing member of the tripartite presidency from the Serb and pro-Russian nationalist Alliance of Independent Social Democrats (SNSD), secured 55.41% of votes, the election commission said. Voting continued in some polling stations after the 7 p.m. (1700 GMT) deadline on Sunday due to delays related to a new electronic balloting system, Bosnia's Central Election Commission head Jovan Kalaba told reporters in Sarajevo. The election commission redesigned ballots and introduced new biometric voter identification and electronic scanners, which it said were aimed at curbing voting fraud. Speaking in Banja Luka, the largest Bosnian Serb city, Milorad Dodik, a separatist and pro-Russian leader of the SNSD who visited Moscow and met Russian President Vladimir Putin last week, said his party's candidate Savo Minic won the most votes for president of the Republika Srpska entity. "We have won the member of the (Bosnian) Presidency, and the president of the Republika Srpska. An unexpectedly high result," Dodik said. Since the Bosnian war ended in 1995 under the US-brokered Dayton peace accord, the country has been split along ethnic lines into two entities linked by the weak central government and tripartite presidency. Bosnia, which has struggled to recover from the 1992-95 war, secured EU candidate status in December 2022 and approval to open accession negotiations in 2024. Actual talks have not started, however, because the domestic legislatures have yet to enact core requirements such as bolstering judicial oversight and passing anti-corruption laws. Borjana Kristo, the deputy head of the Croat HDZ-BiH, said that overall progress could be made through dialogue after the elections. "Bosnia must make progress solely on the principle of consensus, dialogue, and mutual respect," she told party supporters, cautioning against rhetoric that would drag the country backwards. Many voters in the country of 3.4 million people say they want to move beyond divisive rhetoric but its politics have become deadlocked. The EU and Russia have been vying for influence over Bosnia, with the EU seeking to expand its membership across the Balkans while Russia wants to slow that process down and preserve its influence over the Republika Srpska. The US has also sought to bolster its influence in Bosnia, pushing for a $1.5 billion [USN:L6N40Y0SF TEXT:"pipeline project"] to import US liquefied natural gas. The EU has said, however, that the selection of the company for the project lacked competitive transparency, while Washington and Brussels have also clashed over the role of the [USN:L6N41N07W TEXT:"High Representative"], the international peace overseer for the country.

item.title: Ukraine will hit Russian refineries in response to Moscow's 'new doctrine' of airstrikes, Zelenskiy says
item.description: Vladimir Putin called for broader attacks on civilian targets, Volodymyr Zelenskiy told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: Ukraine will double down on attacking Russian oil refineries in response to a new policy of airstrikes by Moscow designed to [USN:L8N44V1KC TEXT:"force people to abandon Kyiv"] and other cities, but will not target civilians, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said. Ukraine's intelligence services has obtained documents showing that Russian leader Vladimir Putin had issued a "new doctrine" of military attacks on a much broader range of civilian targets ahead of this winter, Zelenskiy said. "We saw documents and we know that they allow them to attack infrastructure, logistics, and especially to attack in the cities, in the villages, everywhere, roads, schools, hospitals," Zelenskiy told Reuters in an interview. "To pressure people to leave the capital, leave different cities: this is the goal of the operation." Driving the shift in policy, Zelenskiy said, was Putin's desire to appear strong at a time when his military was losing ground in a key frontline region and sustaining higher levels of casualties. The Kremlin was not available to comment on Saturday. But in a statement [USN:L1N45P03K TEXT:"urging foreign nationals to leave Kyiv"], the Russian Foreign Ministry said Moscow would continue to systematically hit targets in what it said were retaliatory strikes for Ukrainian attacks on Russia in recent months. Both sides deny deliberately targeting civilians. COUNTEROFFENSIVE IN DONBAS Zelenskiy said a successful Ukrainian counteroffensive, code-named "Vivaldi", had recaptured around 140 sq km (54 sq miles) of Ukrain's eastern Donbas region and was still ongoing. Russia has said it must control Donbas in its entirety as a condition for any peace deal. In recent weeks, US President Donald Trump's administration has sought to revive talks to end the four-year-old conflict – Europe's bloodiest since World War Two. The US leader last month urged Ukraine [USN:L1N45503J TEXT:"to refrain from hitting Russian oil installations"], saying that was sending global diesel prices surging. But Zelenskiy, speaking as air raid sirens blared outside the gilded halls of the presidential offices, said he had received no indications from Russia that Putin was interested in peace talks, or discussing a ceasefire on energy infrastructure. Over the past week, the Ukrainian capital has come under persistent attack by Russian drones and missiles targeting energy and telecoms assets, road and rail infrastructure. For the first time, Russia has [USN:L1N45P00Z TEXT:"targeted the bridges"] across the Dnipro river connecting east and west Kyiv. Zelenskiy said Ukraine would react to the change in tactics by Moscow, but would not target civilian infrastructure indiscriminately. "We have to respond in any way (we can). With their attacks on our energy, we have to respond on their energy. First of all, oil refiners etc: what gives money to them for this war," Zelenskiy said in English. "But we will not respond, of course, just like them, on any civilian objects." SUPPORT FROM EUROPE After the Trump administration invited Putin [USN:L6N45F16H TEXT:"to attend a G20 summit in Miami"] in December and discussed business deals with Russian envoys, Zelenskiy urged Washington not to normalise relations with Russia before ensuring a return to peace. Zelenskiy said he would be happy to meet Putin for peace talks at the G20, but he warned the US not to believe in "illusions" that Russia would simply end hostilities if it gained control of Donbas. "It's not fair just to normalise," said Zelenskiy, dressed in his trademark black T-shirt and military-style jacket. Any resumption of economic and diplomatic ties with the West had to be in return for Russia ending hostilities, he said: "Because peace is more important than any kind of economy." While the US has proposed a resumption of trilateral talks in the coming weeks in the UAE, Zelenskiy noted that an exact date and location for the technical-level conversations had still not been set. Ukrainian officials warn that Russia has stockpiled hundreds of ballistic missiles ahead of an expected winter onslaught against electricity and water infrastructure. Last winter, the worst of the war, Russian strikes left swathes of the country without electricity and heating for days at a time. Since the summer, Moscow has also begun launching dozens of fast and relatively cheap jet-powered Shahed drones a day at Ukraine, whose air defence teams have struggled to cope because their interceptor drones were too slow to catch them. Zelenskiy said Ukraine had been forced to rely heavily on its fighter aircraft – F-16s and MiGs – to down around 60% of the Russian jet-powered drones, but supplies of 20 mm ammunition for the planes were running low. Kyiv was urgently working on other solutions – including boosting its electronic jamming capabilities, he said. In the second half of October, it would receive the first shipment of small, cheap air defence missiles capable of hitting the new Shaheds. Last week, Zelenskiy said Ukraine was developing five models of new interceptor drones capable of downing the jet Shaheds. Fresh from a meeting with his defence chiefs, he said tests on two of those models showed a modest success rate of around 30%. "We'll have to scale it," he said. "I hope that with all these things, with all these elements, we'll find a way." BALLISTIC THREAT Ukraine announced the first combat use this week of its own domestically made ballistic missile, the FP-7, which has a range of around 250 km (155 miles). Zelenskiy said he had called the manufacturer Fire Point to pressure executives to finish a longer-range model, the FP-9, which the company has said could hit Moscow. "I said to them, where is my FP-9?" said Zelenskiy, with a grin. "We need the FP-9. And the FP-9 will be (ready) this autumn, I'm sure." Zelenskiy said a recent spate of Russian drone incursions and hybrid attacks in Europe were an effort to intimidate European populations and to undermine support for Ukraine. Some European leaders were starting to understand this, he said, and toughen their position. Russia says such accusations are baseless and the result of anti-Russian hysteria. After talks with European officials in Brussels this week, Ukraine had unlocked funding to order the drones that it needs to keep fighting at the start of 2027, Zelenskiy said. Ukrainian officials had worked on plans with European partners to plug a $27 billion hole in Kyiv's defence budget this year. The plans involve a combination of the reallocation of Ukraine's own budget resources, bilateral assistance and using "money credits" from next year's portion of a €90 billion EU loan, Zelenskiy said. "We will close this (gap). I think this is absolutely a big success for our country," he said.

item.title: KNDS IPO still possible this year, chief tells Handelsblatt
item.description: Franco-German tank maker KNDS could sell its shares this year under the right market conditions, its CEO told the Handelsblatt newspaper on Thursday, after an IPO attempt in July was put on hold.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Franco-German tank maker KNDS could sell its shares this year under the right market conditions, its CEO told the Handelsblatt newspaper on Thursday, after an IPO attempt in July was [USN:L6N43317O TEXT:"put on hold"]. Here are more details: "A market listing in 2026 is still possible, provided that market conditions meet the shareholders' expectations. For KNDS, an early start would be best," CEO Jean-Paul Alary said in an interview. Alary added that a later IPO was also possible, though a transaction during next year's presidential election campaign in France should be avoided. "In the middle of an election campaign would not be the ideal time for an initial public offering. But we’re not there yet," said Alary.

item.title: OFRBS Summary
item.description: Schneider Electric va racheter le spécialiste US des logiciels industriels PTC
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Schneider Electric va racheter le spécialiste US des logiciels industriels PTC 5 octobre (Reuters) - Schneider Electric a annoncé lundi l'acquisition de 100% du capital du spécialiste des logiciels industriels américian PTC, au prix de 205 dollars (183 euros) par action. Pétrole-L'Opep+ maintient ses quotas de production pour novembre LONDRES, 4 octobre (Reuters) - L'Opep+ a décidé de maintenir ses objectifs de production de pétrole pour novembre, a déclaré l'organisation dans un communiqué publié à l'issue de sa réunion de ce dimanche. Renault va investir plus de €10 mds sur cinq ans dans l'électrique en France Le groupe Renault investira plus de 10 milliards d'euros en France au cours des cinq prochaines années dans les véhicules électriques et les voitures plus abordables, a déclaré samedi le directeur général du constructeur automobile, François Provost. Rome réclame des clarifications sur un éventuel départ anticipé de Lagarde de la BCE L'Italie souhaite obtenir des éclaircissements sur les rumeurs concernant un éventuel départ anticipé de la présidente de la Banque centrale européenne (BCE), Christine Lagarde, a déclaré vendredi le ministre de l'Économie, Giancarlo Giorgetti. L'Europe finit dans le vert, le risque d'un resserrement monétaire recule Les Bourses européennes ont terminé en hausse vendredi, l'inflation modérée des indicateurs sous-jacents en Europe et le rapport sur l'emploi américain moins bon que prévu calmant les craintes d'un resserrement monétaire. Wall Street termine en hausse après le rapport sur l'emploi La Bourse de New York a clôturé vendredi en hausse après l'annonce d'un nombre de créations d'emplois aux Etats-Unis bien moindre que prévu le mois dernier, qui renforce la perspective d'un maintien des taux de la Réserve fédérale ce mois-ci. Zone euro: L'inflation s'accélère à +3,8% sur un an en septembre L'inflation dans la zone euro s'est accélérée sur un an en septembre, plus que prévu, dépassant l'objectif de 2% fixé par la Banque centrale européenne (BCE), selon les données préliminaires publiées vendredi par Eurostat. Le rial iranien tombe à un nouveau plus bas, la banque centrale intervient Le rial iranien a poursuivi sa chute samedi, conduisant la banque centrale du pays à annoncer une intervention pouvant atteindre deux milliards de dollars (1,78 milliard d'euros) pour soutenir la monnaie. États-Unis: Chute surprise des créations d'emplois en septembre L'économie américaine a créé moins d'emplois que prévu en septembre, montrent les données officielles publiées vendredi par le département du Travail. La flambée des rendements pourrait atténuer l'impact des prix de l'énergie, selon Rehn (BCE) La flambée des prix de l'énergie rapproche la zone euro du scénario "défavorable" en matière d'inflation esquissé par la Banque centrale européenne (BCE), mais la forte augmentation des coûts de financement à long terme limite son impact sur l'ensemble de l'économie, a déclaré vendredi Olli Rehn, membre du Conseil des gouverneurs de l'institution monétaire.

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: USA-Une résidente de Californie accusée d'espionner pour la Chine un fils du président taïwanais WASHINGTON, 5 octobre (Reuters) - Les autorités américaines ont arrêté dimanche une résidente de Californie accusée d'opérer comme agent étranger clandestin et d'espionner l'un des fils du président taïwanais Lai Ching-te à la demande de responsables chinois, a déclaré le FBI. Brésil/Présidentielle-Bolsonaro, en tête, et Lula s'affronteront au second tour BRASILIA/SAO PAULO/RIO DE JANEIRO, 5 octobre (Reuters) - Le sénateur de droite Flavio Bolsonaro et le président sortant de gauche Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva s'affronteront lors du second tour de l'élection présidentielle au Brésil, a annoncé dimanche soir l'autorité électorale, le premier nommé ayant déjoué les pronostics en devançant l'actuel chef d'Etat. Le président yéménite annonce une offensive d'envergure contre les Houthis 4 octobre (Reuters) - Le président yéménite, dont le gouvernement est soutenu par l'Arabie saoudite, a annoncé dimanche le lancement d'une vaste opération militaire contre les rebelles houthis pro-iraniens, visant à reprendre le contrôle des territoires qu'ils occupent. Des explosions entendues pendant la visite du chancelier allemand à Kyiv KYIV, 4 octobre (Reuters) - Des sirènes d'alerte aérienne et des explosions ont retenti dimanche dans la capitale ukrainienne, Kyiv, alors que le chancelier allemand Friedrich Merz rendait visite au président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky dans le cadre du renouvellement du soutien de l'Allemagne à l'Ukraine. Plus de 500 ex-responsables européens exhortent l'UE à agir vite contre le projet de colonies "E1" PARIS, 5 octobre (Reuters) - Plus de 500 anciens ministres, ambassadeurs et hauts responsables européens appellent lundi la Commission européenne à agir sans délai contre le projet "E1" d'extension des colonies israéliennes en Cisjordanie occupée, en sanctionnant notamment les institutions financières et prestataires de services qui participent à ce programme dénoncé comme "illégal". Les Brésiliens se rendent aux urnes dans un contexte de forte polarisation BRASILIA/SÃO PAULO, 4 octobre (Reuters) - Les Brésiliens se rendront aux urnes dimanche pour le premier tour d'une élection annoncée très serrée, après une campagne marquée par des scandales de corruption, des inquiétudes économiques et des accusations d'ingérence américaine. Espagne-Deux morts dans des inondations en Catalogne 4 octobre (Reuters) - Deux personnes ont péri et une autre est portée disparue à la suite de fortes pluies et d'inondations dans la région de Catalogne, en Espagne, ont rapporté dimanche les autorités. Le Premier ministre letton en passe de diriger une coalition pro-ukrainienne RIGA, 4 octobre (Reuters) - Le Premier ministre letton, Andris Kulbergs, devrait conserver le pouvoir, sa "Liste unie", formation centriste et pro-ukrainienne, étant en passe de signer une large victoire, la plus importante aux élections législatives depuis que la Lettonie a retrouvé son indépendance en 1991. Éthiopie-La capitale du Tigré sous contrôle des forces gouvernementales 4 octobre (Reuters) - Les forces gouvernementales éthiopiennes et les milices alliées ont repris le contrôle de la capitale du Tigré, ont-elles déclaré dimanche, infligeant ainsi un revers majeur à l'alliance d'opposition qui gouverne cette région du nord. L'Ukraine va intensifier ses frappes sur les raffineries russes L'Ukraine va intensifier ses attaques contre les raffineries russes en réponse à la nouvelle stratégie de frappes aériennes menée par Moscou visant à forcer la population à quitter Kyiv et d'autres villes, sans pour autant prendre pour cible les civils, a déclaré le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky.
